Previous challenger brands such as Under Armour, New Balance and Skechers, whose boots are worn by the England captain Harry Kane, have struggled to make an impact on the retail market.

Sports.title: Oxford United apologise for launching ‘United 93’ clothing range around 9/11 anniversary
Sports.content:
Oxford United have abandoned a new range of American style-sportswear after it inadvertently referenced the tragedy of September 11.

The League One club launched their new “Campus Collection” on Friday morning but had removed it from sale by lunchtime, after clothing designs were revealed to bear the slogan “United 93”. The U’s immediately published an apology that admitted to a lack of understanding of “the historical context and associations” related to the branding and made “sincere apologies for this error and any offence caused”.

“Inspired by the style and culture of American sports,” the club originally trailed the Campus Collection as launching on 11 September of this year, the 25th anniversary of the atrocity that killed nearly 3,000 people. Concerns over sensitivity saw the launch then delayed, but when the online collection was finally made available for sale on Friday, images showed models wearing an NFL-style shirt with “United 93” on the chest, in recognition of Oxford being founded in 1893.

United 93 was one of four domestic passenger jets seized by al-Qaida terrorists on 11 September 2001. A mutiny by passengers prevented hijackers from using the plane to destroy a government building in Washington DC, and it ultimately crashed into a field, killing all 44 people on board. A film titled “United 93” was also made about the tragedy.

The Campus Collection was live for approximately two hours on Friday before the webpage was deleted by the club after they realised the meaning of the phrase. “The range was released without understanding of the historical context and associations,” the club statement read. “It should not have reached the point of sale and we take full responsibility for not undertaking proper due diligence.

“We have removed the collection with immediate effect and are reviewing our approval processes to ensure nothing like this happens again. Once again, we would like to put on record our sincere apologies for this error and any offence caused.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Opinion was mixed among Oxford fans, with many outraged but others inclined to forgive the error. One user of the Yellows Forum called it a “monumental cock-up that I would expect to be sacked for if I’d signed off on it”. Another wrote: “Whilst not ideal … everyone who sees this realises there’s no malicious intent. Ultimately there was just no consideration to it at all.”

Sports.title: Why Tottenham are misfiring … and it’s not just down to the lack of goals
Sports.content:
Tottenham have failed to score in their opening four league games for the first time. Two decades have passed since they last drew blanks in four consecutive Premier League matches. While these are outliers, it will take time for Spurs to improve.

Their level of player turnover, from last season to this and from week to week, is a problem. Only four men who played at least half of the league minutes last season have featured in 2026-27. One is Richarlison, who has since been omitted from their Premier League squad. His 15 goal contributions in the league were at least twice as many as any other Tottenham player last season, but he will not be scoring or assisting any time soon.

Richarlison is also the fourth-longest-serving player. Ben Davies, Brandon Austin and Rodrigo Bentancur are ahead of him, and of those only Bentancur is likely to play regularly. Many current starters are relatively new recruits. The 11 players who began the goalless draw with Everton last Saturday had spent an average of 1.3 years with the club. Tottenham have averaged the joint-third-youngest starting XI this season too. They have many players without too much experience, either individually or as a unit.

Roberto De Zerbi has made 12 changes to his starting lineups in the league since the first match, more than any other manager in the division. At four alterations per game, the team is changing more often than it did last season (2.8), when they employed three managers. Little wonder the new-look Tottenham are struggling to gel.

Injuries have not helped, as De Zerbi has mentioned with reference to pre-season. “Micky van de Ven suffered an injury in Australia,” he said. “Domi Solanke the same. James Maddison the same. Mateus Fernandes suffered an injury in Australia. He lost 15 days and it’s not so quick.”

View image in fullscreen Richarlison, pictured against Chelsea in a Sydney friendly, had more goal contributions than any other Spurs player last season – but is not in their league squad. Photograph: Hollie Adams/Reuters

Commercial pressures inevitably influence which countries clubs visit each summer. Chelsea were also in Australia this year, and Aston Villa and Manchester City played friendlies in Asia. But Tottenham were the only club who also went to that side of the world the previous summer. Spurs led the Premier League for days lost to injury in 2025-26 according to Premier Injuries (1,560), with Newcastle (1,271), Arsenal (1,115) and Liverpool (967) also in the top seven; these four clubs were those who went to Asia in summer 2025. High injury tallies may be coincidental but it is fair to question whether another lengthy pre-season trek was right for Tottenham.

Several metrics illustrate their attacking problems. Spurs are capable of getting the ball into dangerous areas, before the next step trips them up.

Their total of 46 completed take-ons leads the Premier League. Only five of these successful dribbles ended with the player creating a chance or taking a shot though. Manchester United have completed 17 fewer take-ons than Tottenham yet have produced tangible output with almost twice as many (nine) chances or shots.

It is similar for high turnovers, which occur when the ball is recovered within 40 metres of the opposition goal to begin a new possession sequence. Spurs have recorded the fourth-most this season (34), but only Coventry (one) have ended fewer of them with a shot (two). Tottenham have produced a goal attempt from 5.9% of their high turnovers when the league average is 19.9%. Nothing is flowing smoothly.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The costliest statistic may concern their productivity in the opposition penalty area. Again, their total of touches in the opposition box – 119, one fewer than Arsenal – looks decent enough. They are often well located to score. But they are taking 3.97 touches per shot in the box, 0.47 more than any other team and 1.15 above average. Everything is taking a beat too long, fatal for many an attacking move.

But look at the makeup of their squad. In terms of Premier League career goals, the 32-year-old left-back Andy Robertson was their top summer signing with 12. Despite being the second-most-expensive transfer in Europe in summer 2024, Solanke still has more goals in the Championship (44) than Premier League (41) and has yet to play the equivalent of 38 full league games for the club across two-plus seasons. Mikey Moore has a quarter of their shots on target (three) in 2026-27, yet played only 90 minutes before going on loan to Cologne.

From once having two of the most accurate shooters in the game in Harry Kane and Son Heung-min, Spurs have filled their roster with men who struggle to hit the proverbial barn door. Most of their squad are at best a few percentage points above league average for shot accuracy, with many of their players below. Chelsea and Bournemouth (24) have had twice as many shots on target as Tottenham this season from no more than nine extra shots in total.

“We have to shoot more, we have to shoot better and we have to finish better the clear situations,” De Zerbi said after the Carabao Cup defeat at Anfield on Tuesday. His team had scored, though an error from Liverpool’s goalkeeper, Giorgi Mamardashvili, played a huge part in Conor Gallagher’s goal. Tottenham cannot rely on opponents making mistakes to bail out their cadre of wasteful attackers. But how long will it take for their mostly young band of new recruits to form an effective unit? Much work lies ahead.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Spying some tasty match-ups, from Wrexham v Saints to desperation derbies
Sports.content:
ENJOY THEM WHILE THEY’RE HOT

Before an engorged international break we have a gala weekend of derby games. Some of them are familiar, others rather longer in the waiting, others spurious in their definition but shoehorned in for tea-timely email purposes. Thursday night’s Bigger Vase defeat by Ferencvaros was not a great result for angry Martin O’Neill’s Celtic, coming three days before the Old Firm/Glasgow derby (delete as applicable according to adherence to Scottish company law), and four days after losing to Rangers in the Old Firm/Glasgow derby. In Spain, Atlético v Real Madrid will see Diego Simeone and José Mourinho bring the morbo ruckus to the sidelines. A football match might actually break out, though that cannot be guaranteed when considering the managers involved.

Plenty of anticipation for Millwall v West Ham, if not from the Met police, which has set up a Section 35 dispersal zone stretching across most of the map on the closing credits of EastEnders. Saturday’s match-up will have rung out when the fixtures came out. That four points separate the two clubs in the battle for promotion has become a side issue. The “Dockers derby”, when supporters’ ancestors worked for rival firms either side of the Thames, hasn’t been played since 2012, the long years since consumed by the cartoon mythology of Danny Dyer, Tamer Hassan and the Rise of the Footsoldier franchise.

Talking of grudge matches, Wrexham v Southampton gained extra Spygate fizz when co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac released a social media disgrace ad for their official web browser (!) on the “importance of privacy”. Those guys! Elsewhere in the Championship, Wolves and West Brom are reunited for a first league fixture in five years, a Sunday high noon kick-off time reflecting West Midlands police’s similar concerns to their London counterparts after a 2024 cup date. Rather more genteel, a university challenge between Oxford and Cambridge, and after Oxon and Cantab split the men’s and women’s Boat Races, there’s first-class honours at stake, in a battle of League One playoff hopefuls.

To a couple of desperation derbies, then. They say you are never more than six feet away from a pest in a big city, and the same logic is true of turmoil at Manchester United and/or Tottenham. Did Michael Carrick shed tears after that Littlewoods Cup defeat by Brighton? Who could blame him? On Sunday United really, really must beat Fulham, for whom Álvaro Arbeloa is taking on the look of lame-duck manager, as well as that of a cross between General Zod and Rylan. If not, Carrick stares down the face of three weeks where “United in crisis” is blood in the water for needy hacks. Maybe Tottenham can provide cover. Their goal drought has been mocked by try-hard pizza companies though perhaps a visit from Aston Villa, whose summer reboot has yielded just one point, can end Spurs’ hosepipe ban.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Scott Murray at 8pm BST for a red-hot updates on Brentford 0-0 Chelsea in yet another weekend derby.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“I got told off for the substitutions I made. Only joking!” – Thomas Tuchel attempts some comedy after being asked what he spoke about with his FA overlords in the post-Geopolitics World Cup review. More impressive was his ability to keep a straight face when he told hacks “99.9% of fans don’t talk about the substitutions I made [against Argentina].” The German recalled Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer in his first squad since the GWC – and even found space for Liverpool’s teenage winger Rio Ngumoha. View the full selection here.

View image in fullscreen Honk! Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

double quotation mark I also met Ludek Miklosko (yesterday’s Football Daily letters), but in a way that now seems rather surreal. When I was a kid, my junior Sunday league team trained at West Ham’s Chadwell Heath training ground every Friday night in their sports hall. In them days, anyone could drive into the car park and walk through the gym to the hall – and on one particular night my dad dropped me and a teammate off and told us he’d be back in an hour. When we walked into the hall we were more than surprised to find that our team had cancelled training, with nobody else turning up, and half of the West Ham first team were in there doing drills instead. With nowhere to go (and no mobile phones) they invited us to join in. As an Arsenal fan, I didn’t really care much for West Ham players, but their goalkeeper was a lovely man and spent most of the hour playing with us and encouraging shots. I never forgot Ludo after that night” – Nicholas Larkin.

double quotation mark I was struck by the sentiment of Christopher D’Cruz that it is not possible to dig yourself out of a hole (yesterday’s letters). OK, I know it is not exactly the same, but it is still a similar principle … they have clearly never heard of Baron Munchhausen pulling himself out of a swamp with his own hair” – Andriy Zavgorodniy.

double quotation mark Christopher has clearly never had to dig a trench, moat, ditch, etc. Sure, there has to be some downward digging to start, but then most of the work is going sideways. Similarly, if you’re stuck at the bottom of a steep-sided hole with nothing but a shovel then the move to get oneself out is digging a gentler slope back to ground-level. Or, to quote the intellectual leviathan, Homer J Simpson: dig up, stupid!” – James Humphries (and 1,056 others).

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Nicholas Larkin. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

Sports.title: Fear and loathing linger as Millwall and West Ham resume ferocious rivalry
Sports.content:
Absence has not made the heart grow fonder. Millwall and West Ham meet for the first time in 14 years on Saturday, but it is not going to be a joyous reunion at the Den. The atmosphere will be ferocious and the main hope is that the focus is on the football rather than any nonsense away from the pitch.

These two have plenty of previous, even though they so rarely play each other. The most glaring example is the shocking disorder inside and outside Upton Park when Millwall lost in the second round of the League Cup at West Ham’s old ground in August 2009. A 44-year-old man was stabbed in the chest as trouble raged outside and riot police struggled to maintain order during the game, with play suspended briefly when home supporters invaded the pitch after one West Ham goal.

View image in fullscreen Police try to control Millwall supporters outside Upton Park station after disturbances following a defeat at West Ham in October 1978. Photograph: PA

There is nothing to glorify here. This will be the 100th competitive meeting, if discontinued, minor tournaments are included, and anyone failing to see the logic behind the rivalry can be forgiven. The sides are not on each other’s doorstep and Millwall are south of the Thames, meaning Crystal Palace and Charlton are more obvious enemies. Yet it is not really about football. The tribalism runs deep, dating back to when the clubs were formed by rival shipbuilding firms at docks on the Isle of Dogs in east London, and is more down to hooligan elements than anything that happens on the pitch.

View image in fullscreen West Ham’s Jack Collison exhorts fans to return to the stands after a pitch invasion at their League Cup tie against Millwall in 2009. Photograph: Stephen Hird/Reuters

There have been many occasions when the nastiness has spiralled out of control. Hooliganism was rife in English football during the 1970s and 1980s and Millwall and West Ham had fearsome firms. Trouble erupted when the sides met at the Den for a testimonial for the Millwall defender Harry Cripps in 1972. The toxicity grew and a Millwall fan, Ian Pratt, died after a clash with West Ham fans at New Cross station in 1976. It is worth keeping in mind when people try to hype up this fixture. Stories about who was top dog on the terraces back in the day are not that interesting.

The 2009 game was disturbing and frightening. In March 2004 there were police horses on the pitch when West Ham fans rioted and ripped up seats during a 4-1 defeat at the Den. Away fans were not allowed in the lower tier when West Ham returned eight months later. West Ham have only 1,774 tickets on Saturday. The Metropolitan police will have measures in place to try to keep opposing fans apart. The dedicated walkway linking South Bermondsey station to the away end acts as a coolant.

The mood will still be tense. There is an odd dynamic to the game. West Ham have at times found it awkward because some of their fans care far more about beating Chelsea and Tottenham. But a trip to Stamford Bridge or N17 is a familiar experience. Going south of the river to Millwall is somehow viewed as different, the short train ride from London Bridge treated as an intrepid journey into some hostile alien planet.

View image in fullscreen Millwall revel in underdog status against West Ham. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

Perhaps the irregularity of the game adds to the mystique. It has happened 18 times in the league since the second world war and only in 1988-89 have the teams been together in the top flight. Millwall stayed up that season but West Ham were relegated, which is usually required for the game to take place. West Ham have generally done something wrong if they are looking for Millwall when the fixture list comes out.

It pits Millwall as underdogs, a role they play well. They often rose to the occasion after West Ham were relegated in 2003. Millwall had a decent team – they reached the FA Cup final in 2004 – and picked up two wins and two draws against West Ham before Alan Pardew led the Hammers back into the Premier League in 2005.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Tim Cahill celebrates Christian Dailly’s own goal as Millwall ran out 4-1 winners at the Den in 2004. Photograph: PA /Alamy

It can be hard for West Ham to match up to the intensity. They won at Upton Park when the sides last met, bouncing back from an early Kevin Nolan red card to beat Millwall in February 2012, but tend to struggle in the away game. The Den is tight, compact, intimidating. Millwall are on a five-match unbeaten run at home against West Ham since losing in 1988. They will look to level the odds. West Ham are on a four-game winning run in the league and top the Championship after smashing Wrexham 6-0 last weekend. Alex Neil’s Millwall came close to winning automatic promotion last season but have injuries and are 10th after an inconsistent start.

Logic says West Ham should win. Logic may not count for very much when the game begins.

Sports.title: Man United's wantaway wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 15, flies to Barcelona for talks amid tug-of-war with Real Madrid after dropping quit bombshell
Sports.content:
Man United's wantaway wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 15, flies to Barcelona for talks amid tug-of-war with Real Madrid after dropping quit bombshell

Manchester United’s teenage star JJ Gabriel held talks with Barcelona on Friday as he prepares to choose between Europe’s top clubs over his next move.

Since Gabriel rocked United with a bombshell demand to quit Old Trafford, it has emerged that he is at the centre of a tug-of-war between Barca and their La Liga rivals Real Madrid.

It’s understood that the 15-year-old winger travelled to Spain via France on Thursday, raising the possibility that his representatives may have spoken to Paris Saint-Germain as well. Bayern Munich are also known to have been tracking his progress.

But Madrid have been leading the chase for Gabriel and are believed to have held talks with his camp over the past few weeks.

Barca made their pitch on Friday and have been keen on Gabriel for some time. The Catalan giants gave him a tour of their club facilities in August 2024 when he was introduced to superstar Lamine Yamal who signed a shirt and posed for a photo.

Manchester City and Chelsea are said to be monitoring the situation, but a move abroad feels more likely at this stage because Gabriel can join a European club two years earlier at 16 due to the fact he holds an Irish passport.

JJ Gabriel has flown to Barcelona for talks over a move to the LaLiga champions

Gabriel (pictured with Lamine Yamal in 2024) has told Man United he wants to leave the club

That would mean United only receiving around £300,000 in compensation, compared to a substantially higher fee if he joined a Premier League rival.

Gabriel has been at United since the age of 11, and is considered one of the hottest young prospects in European football.

The youngster was set to sign a first-year scholarship at United at the age 16 – which would have automatically triggered a lucrative professional contract on his 17th birthday – and could even have made a first-team debut against Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday night.

But he asked United to rip up his current deal which is due to expire at the end of the season. The club have so far refused to do so, but he could go to the Premier League or FIFA to force their hand and become a free agent.

He has not been seen at the club since he scored a hat-trick for the Under-21s on his UEFA Youth League debut against Sabah last week.

United boss Michael Carrick said at his press conference yesterday/on Friday that the youngster’s wellbeing remains paramount regardless of his future at Old Trafford.

‘I think I'd just repeat what I said the other day, really,’ said Carrick. ‘He's a young boy, JJ, and I think it's important that we certainly don't play anything out here. I think the exposure and the scrutiny and everything, you’ve got to be careful and be sensible and think of him as much as anything.

‘So the situation will work itself out, whatever way it's going to work itself out. Making sure he's okay is the important thing.’

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim 'summoned to emergency talks with AC Milan owner' after Europa League defeat amid tough start to life in Italy
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim has reportedly been summoned for emergency talks by AC Milan bosses following his side's Europa League defeat by Benfica. The Portuguese has had a tough start to life in Italy, with his side sixth in Serie A and their boss already throwing shade at his players. Now, according to reports in Italy, Gerry Cardinale, the AC Milan owner, called Amorim for talks, and felt the need to assure him of his future. Gazzetta dello Sport report that Amorim was summoned by his boss for crunch talks this week, and was given a vote of confidence despite his outburst in the week. One of the issues Amorim persistently complained about during his nightmare tenure at Old Trafford was that his players did not suit his style of play, which consists of a back three. And just five games into his new role at AC Milan, the Portuguese coach struck an all-too familiar tone when asked about his squad. Ruben Amorim was summoned by AC Milan officials for crunch talks following his side's Europa League defeat 'I think you are a little bit right,' Amorim told Sky Italia. 'I know at Manchester United and Milan, two big clubs with the pressure to win, people expect everything in just a few months, and I feel the same pressure here. 'I think this team is a little bit different, they are more accustomed to working with three defenders, they are a little bit faster, a little bit stronger. 'Of course, I don't have the clear characteristics that are perfect at this moment, but it is impossible when you take on a new team to have those perfect characteristics right away.' Amorim requested patience and admitted that failure is once again possible, no matter the size of the club. He added: 'I know it will take time, but I also know that there is big pressure at this club, yet I prefer this kind of job because if I need to fail one day, I want to fail big. 'I have a lot of passion for this club, I want to help this club to be better, I don't know if I will have the time, but I look at my players and I think they are listening to everything that I say in training, and that gives me hope we can solve these problems.' Amorim was appointed by Milan in the summer after Massimiliano Allegri's sacking. It comes after he was sacked by United in January, 14 months into his tenure.

Sports.title: 'I went up for a corner at the Old Den and got hit with half a house brick!': West Ham legend JULIAN DICKS on 'horrible' trips to rivals Millwall, the vile (and hilarious) abuse he received and what the Hammers MUST do to win Saturday's clash
Sports.content:
'I went up for a corner at the Old Den and got hit with half a house brick!': West Ham legend JULIAN DICKS on 'horrible' trips to rivals Millwall, the vile (and hilarious) abuse he received and what the Hammers MUST do to win Saturday's clash

Given his status as a West Ham legend and cult hero, it feels appropriate that Julian Dicks is talking about getting hammered.

Not on the pitch and not even in an east London boozer, he means it in the sense of Millwall fans hammering him – by throwing both words and heavy items at him.

This Saturday, the two clubs on either side of the River Thames will play each other for the 100th time but the first in 14 years. It is possibly the fiercest rivalry in the United Kingdom, depicted in the Green Street and Football Factories films as hooligan central.

‘You used to get absolutely f***ing hammered,’ Dicks tells Daily Mail Sport in an interview full of laughs, memories and quite a few F-bombs. ‘And I have no doubt it puts people off their games. No doubt whatsoever.

‘The Old Den was brutal, there was a real hatred. It was horrible. You're coming out of the tunnel, they're spitting on you, they're saying they’re going to kill you, they're going to do stuff to your mum, they're going to give everything towards you. You either f***ing take it to heart or you laugh about it.

‘It's very, very volatile. I remember playing at the Old Den, I think it was 1989 and Paul Ince scored, and I got hit with half a house brick when I went up for a corner!’

West Ham legend Julian Dicks has some colourful memories of playing against Millwall. The local rivals meet this weekend for the first time in 14 years

The former left back made more than 250 league appearances for the Hammers in two stints in the 1980s and 1990s

Ever since West Ham were relegated, this game – which will be free-to-air on ITV at 12.30pm – has been at the forefront of supporters' minds. The Met Police have made special preparations for the match, with officers permitted to remove anyone causing disorder within a radius stretching from Bermondsey to Blackheath, and Wapping to Nunhead.

They will have 400 police on the ground and will use live facial recognition technology to identify potential trouble-makers. In 2009, 54 West Ham fans were banned for life in a League Cup game against Millwall dubbed ‘The Upton Park Riot’.

Dicks knows all about the trouble and hopes the players understand the magnitude of the game. ‘I remember once we beat them 1-0 and us going up to clap our fans,’ explains the former full back, who made more than 300 Hammers appearances and also played for Liverpool and Birmingham.

‘We're walking back and all of a sudden, about 30 police were running up with their batons and shields. I remember thinking, “What the f*** are these doing?”. They've put the shields above our heads because the Millwall fans were just pelting us with everything. Coins, marbles, everything you could think of, it was thrown at us.

'To be honest, I always looked forward to playing against Millwall because you knew that you were in for a game, you knew that the atmosphere would be f***ing horrible and nasty.

‘On the pitch, all the players would give everything they had. They would kick you, they would elbow you, they would do anything to put you off your game. And it's the same with the supporters.

‘I went back to the New Den when I was coaching and I got off the bus and this old girl with a lovely voice shouted to me saying, “Julian? Julian?”. I’ve looked round and she’s said, “You’re a f***ing w****r!”. And she was about 75... You never lose it!

‘And then when my daughter was younger, I walked around where I live with her in a pram and a bloke stopped me in a van. He went, “Are you Julian Dicks? I’m a Millwall fan. I f***ing hate you but I wished you played for Millwall”.'

Dicks is supporting the Every Minute Matters campaign in association with Sky Bet and the British Heart Foundation

‘I went back to the New Den as a coach and this old girl shouted to me: “Julian? Julian?”. I’ve look round and she’s said, “You’re a f***ing w****r!”. And she was about 75...'

Unlike other big rivalries in the UK, such as the Old Firm, this one is not about politics or religion – both sets of fans are very alike and from the same backgrounds. It is hooligan-orientated: wanting to have the hardest firm.

Nuno Espirito Santo’s Hammers had a false start to their return to the second tier, failing to win their first three Championship games, but they have been perfect ever since and travel to the New Den top of the league.

Alex Neil’s Millwall, third last season, are 11th having conceded 13 goals in their last five league outings.

‘There's no reason why West Ham shouldn't win the league,’ adds Dicks. ‘They have a good squad but the only thing that lets teams down is work-rate. Obviously, there's lots of goals in the team of late. But it's about doing it every single game.

‘I go back to Frank (Lampard) at Coventry last season. He didn't have the best players, he didn't have the biggest budget but, f*** me, they worked hard. And they got their rewards.

'West Ham do have a big budget and good players, and now they just need to add that other ingredient.

‘If they do, I have no doubt they will go up. People say it might do them good to go down, it don’t do you no f***ing good, I can tell you! It’s awful to go down but hopefully they bounce back.

Tim Breacker, George Parris and Alvin Martin of West Ham confront Alex Rae of Millwall in a feisty league match in November 1992

The Met Police have been planning for the clash for some time and will have up to 400 officers on the ground around the game

‘Jarrod Bowen will have (father-in-law) Danny Dyer in his ear telling him about all the old days. I remember when I signed from Birmingham, supporters let me know how much this game meant to them.

'I don't mean it in a horrible way, but I used to have fan mail saying: “We want to f***ing beat Millwall, you understand?"

'There is a lot of hatred between the fans. Players like Jarrod know that and hopefully he tells the players. Because, listen, Millwall will be bang up for it.’

As part of the Every Minute Matters campaign, Sky Bet and the BHF have assembled football’s 'toughest ever' five-a-side team to tackle fears around using defibrillators, after 69 per cent of fans said fear could stop them using one during a cardiac arrest. Sky Bet's funding is helping the BHF deliver 400 defibrillators to local communities which will improve the survival chances of around 460,000 people in the UK.

Sports.title: Brydon Carse will NOT face charges as police drop investigation into alleged assault in connection with his nightclub arrest
Sports.content:
Brydon Carse will NOT face charges as police drop investigation into alleged assault in connection with his nightclub arrest

England bowler Brydon Carse will not be charged after an investigation into an alleged assault was dropped by Derbyshire police, according to a report.

Carse, 31, was removed from second Test consideration after being de-arrested following an incident at a Derby nightclub on August 22.

The police said they were looking into allegations of assault. That has now been dropped, according to The Guardian, but it remains to be seen if Carse will be disciplined by England as a cricket regulator investigates.

Carse, who was part of England's squad for the first Tests against Pakistan and their leading wicket-taker during the Ashes defeat in Australia, was released without charge, having been out celebrating with Durham team-mates following their win over Derbyshire in the County Championship.

A short video posted on social media showed Carse, 31, surrounded by four police officers outside the club, with fellow Durham stars Ben Stokes and Matthew Potts in the background. One of the police officers is heard to say: 'Just get him over there'.

The news came not long after England's new Test captain, Joe Root, abolished the team curfew that had been in place since the Ashes defeat in January, insisting his players should be trusted to behave like 'grown adults'.

Police have dropped an assault investigation surrounding England cricketer Brydon Carse

Police previously said the pace bowler was 'de-arrested… having agreed to leave the area'.

Carse had been celebrating Durham's County Championship win over Derbyshire.

Current England captain Root declared himself 'really hacked off' by the latest drinking drama to engulf his side, telling reporters the team must now work hard to regain public trust.

The England and Wales Cricket Board declined to comment.

Sports.title: Liverpool and Leeds legend Gary McAllister, 61, 'faces financial ruin' after being hit with bankruptcy petition - with Scot involved in tax-avoidance scheme alongside fellow ex-players
Sports.content:
Gary McAllister is facing the threat of financial ruin after being hit with a bankruptcy petition by HM Revenue and Customs.

The Liverpool and Leeds legend, 61, has been taken to court by HMRC over an unpaid tax bill, with the amount owed yet to be disclosed.

As reported by the Telegraph, McAllister is understood to have been among a number of high-profile footballers who invested in film partnerships that were subsequently ruled to be tax avoidance schemes by HMRC.

The schemes offered investors substantial tax relief by using relatively modest investments backed by significant loans.

McAllister has not been accused of deliberately evading tax. His representatives say he believed his tax adviser was handling the matter with HMRC and that he is now seeking to bring the dispute to a swift conclusion.

HMRC has spent years pursuing ex-footballers and celebrities involved in the scheme for unpaid tax.

Gary McAllister is facing the threat of financial ruin after being hit with a bankruptcy petition

A spokesman told the Telegraph: 'We take a supportive approach to dealing with customers who have tax debts and do everything we can to help those who engage with us to get out of debt, such as offering instalment plans. We only petition for bankruptcy as a last resort.'

McAllister, who is widely regarded as one of Scotland's greatest ever midfielders, enjoyed a successful career before his retirement in 2004.

He played a key role during Leeds United's title-winning campaign in 1991-92, helping the Yorkshire club win the last ever English First Division before it was rebranded to the Premier League.

After four years with Coventry City in the mid-1990s, the Scottish later joined Liverpool in 2000 and won the FA Cup, UEFA Cup and League Cup over a two-year spell at Anfield.

His career came to an end at Coventry, where he took on the role of player-manager in 2002, having made more than 150 appearances for the club across two spells.

Chalking up 57 caps over his glittering career, McAllister also captained Scotland for four years and famously missed a penalty against England during his country's 2-0 defeat at the 1996 European Championship.

McAllister is one of several former footballers facing the threat of bankruptcy.

Daily Mail Sport revealed earlier this month that HMRC had filed a petition with the High Court to have former Liverpool star Jamie Carragher declared bankrupt over an unpaid tax bill reportedly worth between £700,000 and £800,000.

The Liverpool legend is understood to have been among a number of high-profile footballers who invested in film partnerships that were later ruled to be tax avoidance schemes

Last year, it was also reported that former Liverpool defender Steve Finnan and ex-Manchester City winger Shaun Wright-Phillips were facing separate bankruptcy petitions.

David James, Wes Brown, Lee Hendrie, Trevor Sinclair and John Barnes are among the former Premier League footballers to have been declared bankrupt by HMRC since 2010.

Sports.title: Ineos are failing miserably at Man United. They don't live up to the buzzwords they believe in - and United's utterly nonsensical transfer policy is the proof. No wonder all the clubs they touch are struggling, writes NATHAN SALT
Sports.content:
Every now and then it’s important you refer to the Ineos compass of buzzwords to remind yourself just how much the decision-makers at Manchester United are failing against their very own metrics.

‘If you do a job, do it properly,’ is one of the key messages in the ‘words we like’ half of the compass, a compilation of aphorisms devised by Sir Jim Ratcliffe that features prevalently on the company's website.

‘Wasting time’, ‘losing money’ and ‘don’t do dumb s**t’ all feature in the other half, the ‘words we don’t like’ half.

The Ineos compass tells us a lot. It gives us an insight into the mindset of those running the football side of Manchester United these days.

‘Spend it like it is your own money’ is supposedly a good thing. ‘Making the same mistake twice’, unsurprisingly, is bad.

Then there is ‘walk the talk’, something Ineos are failing miserably on, frankly. ‘Best in class’ is Ineos’ mantra. Yeah, right.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos' management of Manchester United has been a failure in myriad ways, not least their misguided transfer policy over the summer

Ineos' compass of words they do and don't like - words that Ratcliffe is failing to live by

As the boos rained down on United’s players and boss Michael Carrick after a dire collapse from 2-0 up against Brighton to crash out of the Carabao Cup at the first time of asking – again – director of football Jason Wilcox stood aghast in the directors’ box before heading for home.

In light of the Brighton debacle, it is fair to say that Ineos are wasting time, losing money – United do not win a trophy and qualify for the Champions League as things look today – and, with the phased fixing of each position in the team, doing dumb s**t.

No top team in world football subscribes to a model whereby you ‘fix’ one area of the team only per transfer window. Even then, fixes look temporary at best.

Ineos were said to have ‘fixed’ United’s attack under Ruben Amorim when they recruited Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo, ideal player profiles for Amorim’s 3-4-2-1 system as his No 10s. They also recruited Benjamin Sesko to replace Rasmus Hojlund.

They are good players, better than what they had, but none of them are in discussions for being ‘best in class’ in the league.

This summer there was a laser-like focus on overhauling a midfield that lost Casemiro and saw Manuel Ugarte, an Ineos signing that has long been a non-factor in the team, pick up a long term injury.

So, after missing out on their very top targets, they recruited Carlos Baleba for £70million, Andrey Santos for £50m, and Youri Tielemans for £35m. It is too early to judge whether the fix has worked. But the early impressions, with United still so easy to play through, are alarming.

‘Don’t avoid doing the difficult things,’ is another quip on the Ineos compass. And yet they did. They desperately needed a left back, already riding their luck with the fitness of Luke Shaw, and the window closed without one. Negligence that has left the team short.

The defence will get sorted in the summer of 2027, has been the message for many months. Next summer. In a year we’ll fix it. Promise.

Fix it as a Champions League club? Debatable.

Michael Carrick and his players trudge off following United's embarrassing loss at home to Brighton in the Carabao Cup

United left themselves short in the transfer window, reliant on Luke Shaw at left back. Shaw has now missed the last three matchday squads

Carrick has been left with Shaw, who has not played since a designated rest day prior to the Sabah Champions League game a week ago. He has missed the last three matchday squads.

He’s got Patrick Dorgu, signed specifically to fit Amorim’s wing-back system, and is now in a halfway house between not being the first choice left winger and not being a left back.

There’s Noussair Mazraoui, solid enough but not elite at the end of the Premier League United want to be challenging at.

There’s Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro, the latter a £52m Ineos arrival, who both look raw and perhaps haven’t kicked on as ownership hoped at this point.

Matthijs de Ligt hasn’t played for eight-and-a-half months. Diogo Dalot just passed 250 games for United but his deficiencies are as glaring as ever – and some fans after the Brighton game hurled fierce abuse in his direction.

There’s Harry Maguire, still key to propping up this haphazard defensive unit, and Lisandro Martinez, who does often stand up to be counted, and Carrick finds himself navigating choppy waters with a defence that Ineos felt comfortable enough to muddle through with for another 12 months.

A phased rebuild may well be seen as thinking outside the box by Ineos. Zigging where others zag. It may well be that United simply cannot compete financially with the league’s best anymore, a bitterly tough pill to swallow. Or it may be that it’s a nonsensical idea that means one year the floor is broken and the next the roof is caving in and it’s a home that’s never free from problems.

Next summer, when this major defensive rebuild is required, they are still going to have just one main striker on the books in Sesko.

Carrick finds himself navigating choppy waters with a defence that Ineos felt comfortable enough to muddle through with for another 12 months

United are at a stalemate in contract talks with captain Bruno Fernandes. A new deal would require investment that would reduce the budget for a defensive overhaul

They are currently at a stalemate in contract talks with captain and best player Bruno Fernandes. Club sources aren’t panicking, they say, but those two moves would require enormous investment that would obliterate the budget for a defensive overhaul.

Marcus Rashford has been bright since coming back into the fold but if he were to move on at the end of this season another left winger would be required and any managerial change, while not on the agenda this early into the campaign, may well require a totally different skillset and profile for a particular system.

Ineos-owned Lausanne Sport sit bottom of the Swiss league with just one win from eight games.

Similarly Ineos-backed Nice are rock bottom of Ligue 1 with the third-worst defensive record, albeit four games in.

There’s Manchester United Women, they are bottom, too, after a wretched start to the new WSL season.

And then there’s United’s men’s team, who have conceded two goals in three of their four Premier League games so far, are out of the Carabao Cup at the first hurdle and were beaten in the Manchester derby by 10 men. Whatever the opposite of a Midas touch is, Ineos have it.

‘I think the whole standard has dropped at Man United,’ Roy Keane, speaking on The Overlap’s Stick to Football podcast, said.

‘All the decision-makers, the way they’re treating fans, whatever is going on, the women’s team, the standards have dropped throughout the club.

‘What does this team stand for? What does the club, what does Man United stand for? I think all the standards have 100 per cent dropped.’

Ratcliffe's other teams - Nice in France and Lausanne in Switzerland - are both rooted to the bottom of the table

There are coaching issues at play, undoubtedly, and poor player performances to boot.

But Keane is right. The boos that rang around Old Trafford were as much for Ineos as they were for Carrick and the players. Is this really the best in class they vowed to bring to United?

It’s about time those upstairs look at their own moral compass.

Sports.title: Snubbed Premier League star's WAG hits out at Thomas Tuchel after her in-form partner's omission from England squad with Instagram post
Sports.content:
Morgan Gibbs-White's partner has reminded Thomas Tuchel of the Nottingham Forest star's impressive start to the Premier League season after he was snubbed by the England boss once again.

Britney De Villiers shared a statistic on Instagram that Gibbs-White is the only player to have created over five chances in a single Premier League game so far this season - a figure that has seemingly been overlooked by Three Lions boss Tuchel as he selected his 27-man squad for the three-week international break.

Forest captain Gibbs-White is against strong competition for the No 10 position - with Jude Bellingham, Cole Palmer and Eberechi Eze getting the nod ahead of him this time around.

His omission from last summer's World Cup squad raised eyebrows, given Gibbs-White was the top scorer among English players in the Premier League last season.

Morgan Gibbs-White's partner has hit out at Thomas Tuchel's decision to omit him

The England boss once again overlooked the in-form Nottingham Forest star ahead of the next round of international fixtures

Britney De Villiers reminded Tuchel that her partner is the only player to have created more than five chances in a single Premier League game this season

Speaking from Wembley on Friday, Tuchel explained that it 'makes no sense' to select more than three No 10s in justifying his decision to overlook Gibbs-White.

It is not the first time the family of a footballer has taken aim at the German coach.

Following Harry Maguire's shock snub from the World Cup squad, his mother Zoe tweeted 'absolutely disgusted' and 'no words'.

Maguire also shared a pointed statement, believing he had done enough to earn a place on the plane to the United States.

'I was confident I could of played a major part this summer for my country after the season I’ve had,' he said.

'I’ve been left shocked and gutted by the decision. I’ve loved nothing more than putting that shirt on and representing my country over the years. I wish the players, all the best this summer.'

Maguire's mother, Zoe, later tweeted 'absolutely disgusted' in response to Tuchel's decision. She replied to her son's tweet, saying: 'You couldn't have done anymore. Hold your head high ...Disgraceful.'

Maguire's brothers Joe and Laurence also waded into the escalating row, with Joe labelling it 'the worst decision I've ever seen' while Laurence described it as a 'shambles'.

Sports.title: Bill Belichick hits out at 'flat-out lie' about Jordon Hudson in rare interview on 48-year age gap relationship
Sports.content:
Bill Belichick hits out at 'flat-out lie' about Jordon Hudson in rare interview on 48-year age gap relationship

Bill Belichick has given a rare interview to the Wall Street Journal in which he hit back at a 'flat-out lie' surrounding his relationship with Jordon Hudson.

The legendary former New England Patriots head coach, 74, has been dating the 25-year-old former cheerleader since 2023.

Hudson has been a very public presence at the University of North Carolina since Belichick took the job as Tar Heels head coach in 2025.

She has regularly been pictured alongside Belichick on the sideline before games or at practices, and speculation has been rife about the level of her involvement with the program.

Emails uncovered via a Freedom of Information Request last year showed Belichick requesting Hudson be copied into emails to him, raising questions over her role within the program.

UNC has always insisted she has no official involvement with the program - and Belichick has hit out at the 'flat-out lie' that she is involved in all his business.

Bill Belichick has hit out at a 'flat-out lie' about his girlfriend Jordon Hudson

Hudson and Belichick have a 48-year age gap and have been dating since 2023

'I had a lot of other things going on when I took the job,' Belichick told the WSJ. 'So, I sent an email when I got here and I said, "Can you please forward any requests to Jordon about my personal appearances so that I can work and coordinate them outside the university?".

'Didn't have anything to do with the university. Well, that was leaked and released as "Jordon's involved in every single thing that I do and she's copied on every email." That's just a flat-out lie.'

Belichick made it clear any notion she is trying to be heavily involved in the team is 'ridiculous', as he looked to clarify the nature of her role.

'The way the story was picked up was a long way from that,' he said. 'Like, "She's trying to be the general manager of the team." And it's so ridiculous.

'There are some things that she helps me schedule or look at. It's not North Carolina stuff.'

Controversy about the age-gap couple's relationship erupted in April 2025, when Hudson interrupted journalist Tony Dokoupil on 'CBS Sunday Morning' when Belichick was asked how they met.

'We're not talking about that,' she said bluntly from off-camera.

Belichick later criticized the network and claimed the infamous interview was deceptively edited.

Belichick has faced scrutiny over Hudson's level of involvement at UNC

Hudson was back on the sidelines in Chapel Hill last weekend supporting the team

The coach made an appearance on Fox News' podcast 'Hang Out with Sean Hannity' where he said he 'couldn't believe' the treatment he received from the network.

'You know, as we've seen recently, there have been more editing problems, and they go back over a couple of years—multiple examples of editing and interview process and all that,' Belichick said.

'You know, I thought that the interview I had with them was done very deceptively. I've asked for the transcript from them, and they won't give it to me. They've done that with others. I'm not really sure what that policy is.'

Belichick continued, 'I'm kind of confused about some of the things that they [CBS] say they are, but I don't really see them living up to the trust that they talk about.'

When asked by the reporter in the CBS interview how he handles criticism of his relationship with the nearly 50-years-younger Hudson, the former NFL coach replied, 'I've never been too worried about what everybody else thinks. Just try to do what I feel like is best for me and what's right.'

Sports.title: UEFA put pressure on Gianni Infantino by using failed World Cup plan against him
Sports.content:
UEFA put pressure on Gianni Infantino by using failed World Cup plan against him

UEFA are continuing to pile the pressure on beleaguered FIFA president Gianni Infantino, whose World Cup sell-off plan has turned European football's governing body against him

View 2 Images UEFA are leading the fight against Gianni Infantino (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has called for a full review into FIFA's finances and demanded they share £4.5billion cash reserves. Ceferin has written a powerful letter to FIFA president Gianni Infantino suggesting the world governing body dips into its huge wealth and gives each 211 member associations £7.5million each.

‌



It is another step designed to put pressure on Infantino and also get clarity on FIFA's finances after the World Cup sell-off plan. UEFA are demanding Infantino stands down while insisting the sell-off plan highlighted the funds at their disposal and making it clear the associations will get cash whether Infantino remains in charge or not.

‌



Ceferin said: "FIFA must of course remain financially strong, meet its existing commitments and maintain an appropriate buffer, and our analysis takes full account of that. But FIFA currently holds billions of dollars in accumulated reserves.

‌



"These resources belong to football and exist to serve the game and its 211 MAs. Prudence should not prevent a careful examination of whether a portion could responsibly be released to the extent those reserves exceed FIFA's foreseeable needs."

Meanwhile, England boss Thomas Tuchel has backed the FA's stance on Infantino. The FIFA president plans to stand for re-election in March but the FA won't support him.

"I just told you how I am backed from my bosses, so it's the minimum I can do is back my bosses, I would say," Tuchel said. "So they have my full support on that and I back their opinion."

Infantino, 56, has been in the role for 10 years and plans to win a fourth election. Should the Swiss-born chief win, he'll serve until 2031.

‌



Should Gianni Infantino be forced to step down? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin wants to oust Gianni Infantino (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

In a statement issued earlier this month, FIFA confirmed: "The Fifa president announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027. "Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election."

Article continues below

UEFA are confident that a candidate to rival Infantino will be found. The person would need to receive the backing of at least 106 of the 211 FIFA member associations in order to win.

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is understood to be a serious option. Nominations for the presidency must be submitted by November 18.

Sports.title: Man Utd, Liverpool and Chelsea legends to feature in new charity match on free-to-air TV
Sports.content:
Man Utd, Liverpool and Chelsea legends to feature in new charity match on free-to-air TV

A collection of Premier League icons are set to feature in a charity match that will be shown on TV

View 2 Images A new charity match featuring Premier League icons is set to be shown on TV (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

A marquee charity match bringing together Chelsea, Everton, Liverpool and Manchester United legends to face a Rest of the World XI will be broadcast live on Channel 5. The fixture is set to take place on Saturday, September 26, with kick-off at 4.45pm, raising funds for Everton in the Community and Shelter.

‌



The star-studded Merseyside team will be co-managed by Everton legend Peter Reid and Liverpool great John Barnes. The first Game4Hope will now be held at Goodison Park, having originally been pencilled in for Hill Dickinson Stadium.

‌



The home side will come up against a Rest of the World team captained by World Cup winner Rivaldo. He will be joined by his former Brazil teammate Cafu as well as Chelsea icon Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink, Manchester United hero Jaap Stam and legendary Dutch midfielder Clarence Seedorf.

‌



Everton icons Leighton Baines, Gareth Barry, Phil Jagielka, Yakubu, Joleon Lescott and Louis Saha are all set to return to Goodison. The Toffee contingent will be joined by former Liverpool favourites Robbie Fowler, David James, Ryan Babel, Jari Litmanen and John Aldridge.

Sports.title: England boss Thomas Tuchel admits his treatment of Trent Alexander-Arnold was 'unfair'
Sports.content:
England boss Thomas Tuchel admits his treatment of Trent Alexander-Arnold was 'unfair'

Real Madrid star Trent Alexander-Arnold is set to end his England exile over the international break and Thomas Tuchel has made a candid admission after his treatment of the defender

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel has spoken out on Trent Alexander-Arnold's England return (Image: Getty Images)

Thomas Tuchel has admitted that his treatment of Trent Alexander-Arnold has been ‘unfair’ - but not unjustified. The Real Madrid star has played just once under the German coach since his appointment in October 2024 - that solitary outing coming via a 26-minute cameo against Andorra.

‌



Since then, Alexander-Arnold has not been included in a single squad by Tuchel. But he was a surprise name included in the Three Lions’ selection for the upcoming international break.

‌



In explaining his recall, Tuchel has admitted that his treatment of the defender might not have been fair on the defender. Albeit the England boss explained Alexander-Arnold’s exile by suggesting that he had more ‘trust’ in the players who had performed well ahead of the World Cup.

‌



Speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live, the England boss said: “Was it always fair? Maybe not from my side. But if you remember, the next camp was September.

‌



“We were suddenly flying and we stuck to the same squad in October and that was it for him. There was never a chance for him to come back whether that was for or not. I just trusted the guys who were in camp.

“And I had evidence for it. Jordan Henderson said it so, so impressively well before the match against France. You just never know when your next England match is coming so guys this is it, this is the next England match.

“You play with the fullest, you show up with the right attitude and you give it all because you never know.

‌



“It’s not even a shout-out to Trent, it’s a shoutout to everyone that’s a mentality that we want to have. You come to camp, it’s not an international break, it’s an international window. This is important and this matters.

View 2 Images Trent Alexander-Arnold has not played for England since June 2025 (Image: Getty Images)

“You don’t come to relax. You don’t come to take a break. You come to perform and it;s difficult to perform for England and the guys who perform now have our trust. And the guys who come new into camp, we demand the highest of them. It includes Trent but it’s not exclusively for him. It’s for everyone who comes to our camps.”

Article continues below

In all, Alexander-Arnold has earned 34 caps for England since his debut under Gareth Southgate in 2018. In that time, he has scored four goals.

His return to the Three Lions fold comes after a somewhat difficult debut campaign with Real Madrid where he made just 35 appearances for the Spanish giants. He has made three starts under new boss Jose Mourinho this term.

Sports.title: Jordan McCann QUITS boxing after KO defeat to 'UK's Hardest Man'
Sports.content:
Jordan McCann QUITS boxing after KO defeat to 'UK's Hardest Man'

The Manchester rapper has called time on his boxing career just days after suffering a brutal defeat to the 'UK's Hardest Man' - also known as Big Stacks

View Image Jordan McCann shows off his injuries just days after losing to big Stacks

Jordan McCann has officially QUIT boxing just days after losing to the 'UK's Hardest Man.'

‌



McCann and the 'UK's Hardest Man' - commonly known as Big Stacks - finally settled their rivalry months after the former had sucker-punched Stacks in the build-up to a Misfits event earlier this year.

‌



The pair clashed in Newcastle on Saturday night - with Stacks, real name Charlie Robert, using his size advantage early after repeatedly landing jabs on McCann. The Manchester rapper was struggling to see out of his right eye and when the fight was paused in the second round for it to be inspected, the doctor had no option but to wave off the contest, handing Big Stacks the win.

‌



On Friday afternoon, McCann took to social media to show off his battle scars following his clash with Big Stacks and revealed to his fans that he would not be fighting again. "A week after the fight now. I do not look too bad you know what I mean?" he began.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Conor Benn has world title shot shut down just days after Ryan Garcia loss READ MORE :

"But, I really had a good time doing the Misfits. I really appreciate it and I appreciate Mams (Taylor) and stuff. But yeah, I will not be doing that again. Not that I am scared or nothing.... but I still process like... it's good. It's a very good thing to get in and get out. Got a main event in my second fight, took over the show. That's always my plan, but it's just not for me. I have always been online with my music.

"It's just to be happy and do music and do whatever. Calling people names and targeting people and bullying people, it's not my way. It has never been my way my whole life. Just the whole process, the people you have to deal with... it's not for me. I am focused on my music now. I have had two fights - got some good money off it. And yes, I just want to say thanks to Misfits, thanks to everyone... but I am the worst boxer that ever lived. I am no good."

McCann's loss to Big Stacks marked his second defeat under the Misfits banner after he was beaten by Ibiza Final Boss on his debut earlier this year. Stacks had lost a comical 'body shot only' bout with Armz Korleone earlier this year before picking up his first Misfits win against McCann.

Article continues below

When asked who he wanted to fight next, he called out Martyn Ford, who is also known as the World's Strongest Man. "I'm the hardest man and I'm here to stay," he said. "Martyn Ford, he's a big donut; I want him next. He's big but he's a prick. I want to smash his head. I want to kick his head in."

Sports.title: Fabian Hurzeler doubles down on Arsenal comments after criticising champions
Sports.content:
Fabian Hurzeler doubles down on Arsenal comments after criticising champions

Arsenal are set to take on high-flying Brighton this weekend just a few months after Seagulls boss Fabian Hurzeler had some less than complimentary comments about the Gunners

View 2 Images Fabian Hurzeler will be reunited with Mikel Arteta this weekend (Image: Getty Images)

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler has refused to back down from his comments that Arsenal ‘make their own rules’. The Brighton boss made the jibe when assessing the Gunners last term on their way to lifting the Premier League crown.

‌



He had been left furious after a 1-0 defeat in March, as he claimed that there was only ‘one team who tried to play football’. Speaking at the time, Hurzeler said: “If they win the Premier League, no one will ask how they win the Premier League. You can really feel that they do everything now to win and, in the end, it’s about the rules.

‌



“So if the Premier League, if the referee, allows everything, then it’s difficult. Then, they make their own rules. At the moment, I have the feeling they are doing their own rules, no matter how they are playing. I will never be that kind of manager who tries to win in that way.

‌



“Of course, every team will manage and waste time but there has to be a limit and the limit has to be set by the Premier League. The limit has to be set by the referees. At the moment, they just do what they want.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Hurzeler was asked about his comments ahead of this weekend and claimed that his opinion still stood. Speaking in his pre-match press conference, the German said: "Last season was last season. Opinions are important and I will always share my opinion if I am asked.

"But I congratulated Arsenal for being deserved champions. It's a new season. They started very impressively. It is our challenge to compete with them."

Arsenal could keep up their 100 per cent record with a victory at the Amex Stadium on Saturday afternoon, albeit are in for a tough challenge against a Seagulls side sitting fifth in the early Premier League table.

‌



View 2 Images Fabian Hurzeler launched an astonishing rant last season about Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

On Hurzeler and his comments, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said: “That’s all done, that’s all in the past. I have huge respect for Fabian, what he’s done and what Brighton have done as a club, it’s just remarkable. Tomorrow is going to be a beautiful game to watch, I’m sure.”

Following the clash with Brighton, the Premier League will take a back seat ahead of the first international break of the campaign. Should the Gunners win and results go for them this weekend, Arteta’s side could head into October top of the table.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel flies in for transfer talks with Barcelona after Man Utd respond to request
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel flies in for transfer talks with Barcelona after Man Utd respond to request

Manchester United academy star JJ Gabriel has been in the spotlight ever since his shock request to leave Old Trafford this week

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel is keen to leave Old Trafford (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel has reportedly arrived in Barcelona for talks. It comes just days after he stunned Old Trafford chiefs with his request to have his registration with the club cancelled, something United have rejected.

‌



The academy star could have been in line for his first-team debut at United on Wednesday night. The Red Devils had planned to include Gabriel in their squad to face Brighton & Hove Albion in the Carabao Cup third round. It would have made the 15-year-old United’s youngest-ever first-team player.

‌



But that did not happen after his stunning request was made earlier this week. Concern grew over Gabriel after he deleted all pictures on his Instagram profile last week. The unusual behaviour came without any explanation, but his desire to leave may offer one.

‌



JJ Gabriel snubbed for England youth call-ups days after Man Utd star demanded to quit READ MORE :

Michael Carrick points blame for Man Utd struggles and responds to sack question READ MORE :

Now, Barcelona are set for talks over a potential deal. Fellow European giants Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich are also interested.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Gabriel's camp submitted a formal request for United to deregister him this week, but it was denied. The club are still trying to convince him to stay at the club.

‌



However, that looks increasingly unlikely now that Gabriel and his entourage are in Spain. The player could hold talks with Real as well as Barca over a transfer next month.

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel's time at Man United looks to soon be up

Although United have Gabriel under contract until the end of this season, there is a precedent for him to move abroad after he turns 16 on October 6 if he holds an EU passport, exploiting a FIFA loophole to sign for the La Liga giants.

‌



He could qualify for that through his father's Irish connections or his mother's Cypriot background and reports in Spain suggest he will obtain the relevant documentation to complete a move next week.

United could then be powerless to prevent it, although any move would still require FIFA approval. United can offer scholarship terms to Gabriel from his 16th birthday and although he now appears certain to leave, doing so should ensure they receive modest compensation.

‌



Red Devils head coach Michael Carrick was asked for an update on the situation at his press conference after the dismal Brighton defeat on Wednesday night.

The 45-year-old said: "I just think we've got to be really careful of the whole situation, you know.

"He's a young boy, he's 15, and for me, definitely, and from a club point of view, is looking after our younger players, their welfare, their well-being, their exposure, and I think we've got to be really, all of us, I think we've got to be really conscious of that, really, in this situation."

Article continues below

When Carrick was asked whether he gets involved with conversations over Gabriel's future, or leaves it to club chiefs, he responded: "No, as a club for sure, we're all involved in those conversations. I just think we've got to be very careful, you know, of that."

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel won't be playing for England in the upcoming international break (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Lee Carsley's Under-21 side play their final three UEFA U21 Euro qualifiers and have an opportunity to secure their place at next summer’s finals in Albania and Serbia.

Sports.title: Aidan O'Brien tips Darkness Falls as first Triple Crown hope since Camelot
Sports.content:
Aidan O'Brien tips Darkness Falls as first Triple Crown hope since Camelot

Darkness Falls delivered an impressive victory at the Irish Champions Festival, with trainer Aidan O'Brien now eyeing the 2,000 Guineas, Derby and St Leger, a feat that just eluded Camelot in 2012

View 3 Images Darkness Falls: on Triple Crown trail (Image: Evan Treacy/PA Wire)

Aidan O'Brien reckons his stunning Irish Champions Festival victor Darkness Falls might be his first genuine Triple Crown prospect since Camelot.

‌



Camelot famously fell short of becoming the first horse since Nijinsky in 1970 to claim the 2000 Guineas, Derby and St Leger when beaten by Encke in the final leg back in 2012. John Oxx's Sea The Stars captured the Guineas and Derby three years prior, but Doncaster's final Classic of the season was never truly considered as he concluded his outstanding career in the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe the following month.

‌



Nearly 60 years have passed since Nijinsky conquered British Flat racing's ultimate prize, but O'Brien believes he may have discovered another contender, one fittingly sired by Camelot himself.

‌



Value Scope: Each way horseracing tips from Steve Jones for Saturday on ITV READ MORE :

Grand National-winning trainer backed by Kia Joorabchian for new chapter READ MORE :

"Darkness Falls could be our first Triple Crown horse since Camelot. He looks to have the capacity to stay, he has that speed," he revealed. "The next place to go with him is the thing. Do we go to the Dewhurst or the Futurity Trophy? It's possible he could go to the Dewhurst, he could have the pace for it.

"He is unusual, he has a super mind, he's a great traveller and he quickens so we'll see how he is, but he's obviously really exciting."

Constitution River had been O'Brien's standout hope this season, following victories in the French Guineas, French Oaks and the Eclipse. However, back-to-back defeats at York and in the Irish Champion Stakes have tarnished his standing, raising the possibility of a drop back to a mile for the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes at Ascot.

‌



View 3 Images Constitution River: lost unbeaten record at York (Image: PA)

O'Brien commented: "There's a chance that we've been doing the wrong thing with him and he's the miler and Gstaad is the mile-and-a-quarter horse. They are both top colts, we just have to decide with him do we go to Ascot."

He added: "It's possible he could go to the mile, and does Gstaad go to Ascot and go up to a mile and a quarter (Champion Stakes)? At the start of the year we always thought he would go up (in trip)."

‌



In contrast, Sun Goddess more than delivered on her promise last weekend, storming to a commanding win in the Moyglare Stud Stakes.

"Sun Goddess looks a freak, that's all you can say," O'Brien enthused. "There was a good chance she wouldn't get the seven (furlongs) but instead of it exposing her it exposed everybody else. If everything is well she could go back for the Cheveley Park, why not."

View 3 Images Minnie Hauk: could run in the Arc (Image: Getty Images)

‌



With the Arc on the horizon, O'Brien's squad appears less formidable than it did earlier in the campaign, though he could still field a strong contingent, particularly as a number of his horses have been battling a mild infection.

"Benvenuto Cellini, we felt in the race in France (fifth in Prix Niel) the pacemaker went off and none of the others followed him so it became a tactical race which didn't suit him," O'Brien explained.

"He did give a few coughs for a few days when he got back. His coughing is starting to disappear, but his scoping is perfect and he should be fine come Arc time if the ground is nice, if not he'll go to America.

Article continues below

"Minnie Hauk will probably go to the Arc and it looks like she'll be at her best of the year come Arc weekend as long as she doesn't give a cough or anything. Diamond Necklace is in great shape, she has a choice of either the Arc or the Prix de l'Opera, she is in good order.

"I might have backed her up too quick in Deauville and not had enough respect for the competition. I thought she would win, but she got a bit tired in the bad ground so she's probably better than that."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
