World.title: KBR and AKT sign engineering deal for Iraq’s West Qurna gas capture project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – KBR and AKT have signed a contract to complete the comprehensive engineering design for Iraq’s West Qurna Gas Capture Project, which advances Basrah Gas Company’s efforts to collect associated gas and minimize flaring in southern oilfields.

KBR will offer engineering expertise for the design work in partnership with AKT, since the project is part of Basrah Gas Company’s (BGC) larger gas collection initiative.

The project aims to collect associated gas generated with crude oil from West Qurna, which would otherwise be burnt, enabling more of the resource to be processed and consumed domestically.

Expanding gas capture is critical to Iraq’s attempts to prevent flaring, enhance local gas supplies, and make better use of its energy resources, especially as the country seeks to reduce its dependency on imported gas and fuel for power production.

The West Qurna development is one of many gas projects now underway in southern Iraq, where some of the country’s major oilfields are located and significant amounts of associated gas are generated.

KBR said that the deal strengthens its role in gas monetization and energy infrastructure projects in Iraq and the broader Middle East.

The companies did not disclose the contract’s amount or the timeframe for completing the detailed engineering design.

World.title: Iraq PM to meet Trump in New York as US ties shift to investment
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi will visit the United States next week to address the UN General Assembly and meet with President Donald Trump, as Baghdad aims to pivot its relationship with Washington away from security cooperation and toward long-term commerce and investment.

According to government spokesperson Haider al-Aboudi, Al-Zaidi will give Iraq’s presentation to the UN General Assembly in New York, as well as meet with Trump and other international leaders.

He is also slated to attend an economic-related conference of the United States Chamber of Commerce.

The trip comes barely two months after Al-Zaidi’s first official visit to the United States, during which Baghdad announced 48 agreements and collaborations with American corporations spanning energy, infrastructure, technology, healthcare, and finance.

During discussions in Washington and Houston, Al-Zaidi advocated for more US investment in Iraq and met with leaders from key American corporations.

According to the US Chamber, the agreements and memorandums announced during the visit were worth more than $60 billion and included corporations such as Chevron, ConocoPhillips, GE Vernova, Google, JPMorgan Chase, and PepsiCo.

Al-Zaidi also met with Chevron officials in Houston as Iraq explored agreements for large oilfields and new export infrastructure aimed at diversifying the country’s pathways to international markets.

The current visit takes place only days before the conclusion of the US-led coalition operation in Iraq on September 30.

Al-Aboudi regarded the date as a watershed moment for Iraqi sovereignty, stating that relations with Washington will shift toward long-term economic collaboration, boosting Al-Zaidi’s desire to make investment and private-sector links the basis of the next phase of the Iraq-US relationship.

World.title: Palestinian state more distant than ever, a year after recognition
World.content:
Ramallah – When France, Britain and other Western powers last year recognised a Palestinian state, entrepreneur Adam Bader felt a sense of hope.

“I was happy when I heard about it,” said Bader, 27, who lives in the occupied West Bank’s city of Tulkarem, which has seen repeated Israeli raids in recent years.

“Now a year on, we’re not seeing any improvement. On the contrary,” he said. “The situation is getting worse by the day and no one can do anything.”

A year after the recognition, Palestinian statehood in real, tangible terms looks more distant than ever.

Israeli settler violence has soared, Palestinians are being pushed into ever-smaller areas and the Palestinian Authority has only been weakened.

French President Emmanuel Macron, vowing to find a new path forward amid global outrage over Israel’s offensive in Gaza, on September 22, 2025 led a special UN summit to recognise a Palestinian state.

Ten countries, also including Britain, Canada and Australia, recognised Palestinian statehood, bringing the number of UN member-states doing so to around 157, more than four-fifths of the UN membership.

But Israel, which enjoys support from the United States, adamantly rejects Palestinian statehood, and has stepped up efforts to isolate the Palestinian Authority of president Mahmoud Abbas.

While Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stopped short last year of formally annexing the West Bank, observers say unofficial annexation is creeping as his right-wing government approves an unprecedented number of settlements.

“Recognition makes the two-state solution a reality politically and diplomatically, but unfortunately on the ground it still depends on the illegal behaviour of Israel, which is not implementing international resolutions,” Omar Awadallah, deputy foreign affairs minister of the Palestinian Authority, told AFP.

Ines Abdel Razek, a Palestinian political analyst, said that recognition of a state of Palestine amounted to little without measures to support its existence and counter Israeli actions.

“The two-state solution’s become a diplomatic refrain to avoid looking at reality in the face,” she said.

– ‘No future’ –

Across the West Bank’s limestone hills, thousands of Israeli flags line roads used by Israeli settlers, with the occasional graffiti “No future in Palestine” stencilled on walls, as a call for Palestinians to leave.

Netanyahu argues that a Palestinian state would be a “reward for terrorism” after Hamas on October 7, 2023 carried out the deadliest attack ever on Israel, which responded with a massive military operation in Gaza.

“As long as I am prime minister, an Iranian-controlled Palestinian state will not be established — neither in Gaza nor in Judea and Samaria. Period,” Netanyahu said last month, using the biblical name for the West Bank.

Iran, which the United States and Israel attacked in February, backs Hamas in Gaza. The Palestinian Authority, centred in the West Bank, is led by Fatah, Hamas’s archrival.

Ahead of the anniversary, Israel ordered the closure of the UK consulate serving Palestinians from Jerusalem, angered after Britain led France and Canada in sanctions over rising attacks by settlers.

Foreign Minister Gideon Saar, explaining the move, said Britain’s Labour government was attempting to “force upon Israel” a Palestinian state but the attempt was “doomed to fail”.

– Rising attacks –

The Palestinian Authority, established in the 1990s, has been starved of cash in part by Israel’s decision not to give it customs revenue it collects on its behalf, and struggles to pay its civil servants.

Israel has objected to the Palestinian Authority’s historic payments to families of imprisoned or slain Palestinians, including those who carried out attacks against Israelis.

In early 2025, Israel built nearly 1,000 gates in the West Bank, at the entrances of nearly all villages and towns, which it closes on occasion to control Palestinian movement.

Palestinians have also decried a policy of “maximum land, minimum Arabs” whereby settlers push out isolated herder communities from rural areas in order to establish settler outposts.

The UN says extremist settlers have been responsible for an average of six attacks per day on Palestinians and Palestinian property in the West Bank in 2026.

Palestinians complain that Israeli perpetrators of violence are almost never brought to justice, and are protected by the army.

Defence Minister Israel Katz has called for police to take over civilian matters from the military in the West Bank, a move observers see as a further step towards annexation.

Sameh, a software engineer in Nablus, still sees last year’s move as a positive sign, but concedes the difficulties.

“There is still a big distance between international recognition and seeing that recognition translated into reality on the ground,” he said.

MoHUA Secretary D Thara

NEW DELHI: There is a need to write the âintentâ of policies, regulations and guidelines in brief while notifying them, a move that will bring clarity and communicate what it aims to achieve, suggested D Thara, secretary of newly created department of capital development under the housing and urban affairs ministry.Speaking at a conference of the real estate sector by Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Thara said people making policies often assume a policy has been communicated clearly, only to find that it is interpreted in completely different ways by different stakeholders depending on their interests or perceived gains and losses.She said that communicating an intent is a âvery big challengeâ for policymakers. âFor example, we write a single sentence and we are thinking we have communicated this and then later we found out that it had just the opposite interpretation in some other quarter... So Iâm just wondering how do you bring out that clarity as to what is the intent? Intent is more important than what the sentence communicates.Thara said that henceforth her department will adopt the practice of writing a small intent before going on to the real policy prescription. âI think one reform we should all adopt in govt is this,â she addedThe official also urged the real estate developers to work closely with city municipalities to create necessary physical infrastructure for their residential and commercial projects.She also urged builders to focus on rain harvesting, water recycling and sewage treatment among other critical facilities.âEvery development creates an interaction with the larger urban environment, and we need to understand and mitigate the externalities that construction can create for the city,â she said. Calling for a new public-private paradigm in urban development, Thara asked real estate developers to work more closely with municipal agencies and assess the impact of every project beyond its boundaries - from the water it displaces and the sewage it generates, to the energy it consumes and the infrastructure it requires.

World.title: Punjab govt announces 8 pc DA hike for employees, pensioners
World.content:
CHANDIGARH: Ending a prolonged standoff with state employees, the Bhagwant Mann government on Friday announced relief for around eight lakh employees and pensioners, increasing the Dearness Allowance (DA) by 8 per cent.

The decision followed a meeting held here between chief minister Bhagwant Mann and representatives of employee and pensioners' organisations.

Ministers Aman Arora and Baljeet Kaur, chief secretary KAP Sinha, secretary general administration KK Yadav and others were also present.

After the meeting, Gurnam Singh Virk, president of Punjab State Ministerial Services Union, said the enhanced DA will be given from October 1.

He said, regarding various other issues, the government has also assured them that these will be discussed soon.

The deadlock began August 27 when over three lakh government employees went on a statewide strike by availing mass casual leave, pressing the state government to accept their various demands, including release of their pending 18 per cent Dearness Allowance.

An official statement quoting Bhagwant Mann said the move reflects his government's commitment to the welfare and dignity of employees, whom he described as the backbone of the state's administrative machinery.





The chief minister also announced compulsory monthly meetings with employee representatives to address genuine issues, postings for women employees within 40 kilometres of their homes, and highlighting that around 70,000 government jobs have been provided through a transparent and corruption-free process.

Women employees should not have to choose between their career and their family responsibilities.

The state government will ensure that the system remains sensitive to their genuine needs, he said.

Mann met representatives of employees and pensioners, heard their concerns, it said.

After the meeting, Mann stated on X: "Had a very positive meeting today with employee and pensioner organisations. Employees are an important part of our family, and keeping their welfare in mind, we have immediately decided to increase the Dearness Allowance (DA) by 8 per cent.

This increase will start reflecting with the October salary".

"We also discussed long-pending issues inherited from previous governments, including the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), salary during the probation period, and issues concerning ASHA and Mid-Day Meal workers. We will meet again in the first week of October to work towards a permanent resolution of these longstanding issues.

"There is no distance between our government and employees.

We will resolve every issue through mutual dialogue. We will continue to work together for Punjab's progress," he said.

Emphasising that the welfare, dignity and legitimate concerns of government employees remain a priority for his government, Mann said, "As per the decision, two instalments of 4 per cent each will be released to employees and pensioners, with the benefit to be reflected in their salaries from October 1.

Ahead of the festive season, this decision will provide additional financial support to thousands of government employees and pensioners and their families.

"

The chief minister said, "The government understands the responsibilities shouldered by its employees and the pressures they face in their personal and professional lives."

"A happy employee is a productive employee and I believe that when an employee works with satisfaction, dignity and peace of mind, the entire system performs better and the people receive better services...".

"The state government has an open mind towards the genuine demands of employees and pensioners and these issues will be examined sympathetically and in accordance with the applicable rules, financial implications and legal position."

He said the government will examine various long-pending demands, including "the demand for a 2.59 pension multiplication factor, restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), restoration of various allowances, implementation of Assured Career Progression (ACP), issues relating to the 2015 and 2020 letters concerning the probation period, generalization of court decisions and others."

"No genuine issue concerning employees is being ignored and the government will examine each matter with an open and sympathetic approach. Employee welfare cannot be treated as a one-time exercise and requires continuous dialogue between the government and its workforce," he said.

World.title: Maldives settles $150m India loan; final $50m tranche paid after six extensions
World.content:
The Maldives has fully repaid a $150 million Treasury bill facility subscribed by the State Bank of India (SBI) in 2019, with the final $50 million tranche settled on September 17, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said on Friday.

MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the facility had been extended six times, with the final tranche marking the completion of the repayment.

âThe final tranche of US dollars 50 million Treasury bills, out of a total of US dollars 150 million subscribed by the State Bank of India with the Government of Maldives, has been successfully settled on 17th September,â Jaiswal said at a media briefing.

The $150 million Treasury bills were subscribed by SBI in 2019 as part of financial support to the Maldives.

While the Maldivian government repaid the principal, India covered the interest costs associated with the facility.

âIt may also be noted that while the principal amount of the Treasury bills was paid by the Government of Maldives, the interest payment of all the US dollars 150 million Treasury bills over the past five years was borne by the Government of India,â Jaiswal said.

âThe total amount paid by India in interest settlement was close to US dollars 45 million,â he added.





The repayment comes as the Maldives continues to manage its debt obligations and foreign exchange position. Its Ministry of Finance said the government had made arrangements to ensure that debt servicing would not disrupt imports of essential commodities, including fuel, food and medical supplies.

âThe Government has also put in place the necessary arrangements to ensure the continued availability of foreign currency for the import of essential goods, including fuel, food items and medical supplies,â the ministry said.

âSafeguarding the uninterrupted supply of these essential goods and services remains a key priority of the Government.â

India continues to provide financial support to the Maldivian financial system. Jaiswal said New Delhi had extended an Rs 30 billion currency swap facility to the Maldives, while SBI has subscribed to $350 million worth of Maldivian Treasury bonds valid until 2029 and 2030.

The MEA also said the two countries continue to cooperate on development projects and supplies of essential commodities.

The Maldives government, meanwhile, said it was continuing discussions with international financial institutions and bilateral partners to strengthen its foreign exchange position.

World.title: CM Vijay to launch one-gram gold ring scheme for babies born in Tamil Nadu govt hospitals
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay will launch the one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns on September 28, the state government said. The one-gram gold rings will be provided to babies born in government hospitals under the scheme.

The rings will have a unique serial number and be packed in tamper-proof packaging, the government said. As many as 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings have been procured for the first instalment of the scheme.

The government said beneficiaries must be permanent residents of Tamil Nadu to be eligible for the one-gram gold ring scheme.

Vijay had announced the one-gram gold ring scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of âThaimaaman Seerâ.

The scheme will have retrospective effect from June 22, Vijayâs birthday. A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of âThaimaamanâ.

The state has allocated around Rs 755.83 crore annually for the scheme, which will cover newborns delivered at government institutions. The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings and supply them based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee the implementation and monitoring of the scheme.

Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.

World.title: Mamata gets 'footballer', but can she win TMC 'khela'? Maharashtra has a red-card warning
World.content:
For 28 years, TMC has been

and

has been TMC in West Bengal; the two are almost synonymous with each other. And for voters, the political shorthand for Mamata Banerjee has been almost absurdly simple: two flowers on grass.

Now, that shorthand has been taken away.

The Election Commission on Friday allotted Mamata's faction a new name - 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress', with a football player as its symbol. The rival Arup Roy faction will contest as 'Democratic Trinamool Congress', with an 'envelope' as its symbol. The decision follows the commission's September 17 order freezing the original All India Trinamool Congress name and its reserved 'flowers and grass' symbol for the upcoming bypolls.

Mamata Banerjee is now fighting to save her own party name and symbol.

But the EC's interim arrangement is only the first chapter. The substantive question of who gets the original TMC name and symbol will have to be decided under Paragraph 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.

And here, the story might look familiar.

The same movie was played out twice in Maharashtra in recent years, first with the Shiv Sena and then with the Nationalist Congress Party.

They do not know that I cannot leave TMC. It will always be with me until I leave this world. Absolutely dirty game, but we are also ready to fight it out. I want the BJP to go from India. We want solidarity in INDIA alliance. Mamata Banerjee

What Shiv Sena and NCP cases tell us

When Shiv Sena split between Uddhav Thackeray and Eknath Shinde in 2022, the EC first froze the party's 'bow and arrow' symbol and allotted separate interim identities to the two factions.





In its February 2023 decision, the commission eventually recognised the Shinde faction as the Shiv Sena and allowed it to use the original name and symbol.

The NCP followed a similar path. After Ajit Pawar's rebellion in July 2023, the EC decided in February 2024 that the faction led by Sharad Pawar had a weaker numerical claim, while Ajit Pawar's group had superior support in the organisational and legislative wings.

It consequently recognised Ajit Pawar's faction as the NCP and allowed it to use the party's 'clock' symbol. The EC order specifically recorded that the Ajit Pawar group had "far superior numerical support" in the organisational and legislative wings.

That is a crucial part of the precedent for the ongoing TMC dispute.

The conclusion from the Maharashtra cases may be that the EC followed the majority of legislators.

The legal position is more nuanced. Paragraph 15 allows the election commission to examine rival claims through the party's organisational structure as well as its legislative strength.

In its May 11, 2023 Constitution Bench judgment in Subhash Desai vs Principal Secretary, Governor of Maharashtra, the Supreme Court held that the EC need not determine a party's identity solely through the numerical strength of its MLAs or MPs while adjudicating a dispute under Paragraph 15 of the Symbols Order.

The court said the EC could consider the majority in the organisational wing, the party constitution and, where appropriate, "any other appropriate test", underlining that a split among legislators is not necessarily the same as a split in the political party itself.

The timeline of TMC split.

The observation is particularly relevant to the TMC case, where the eventual contest could involve competing claims over the party's organisational structure and not just a headcount of elected representatives.

The Supreme Court, however, did not itself decide which faction should receive the Shiv Sena's name and symbol, leaving the merits of that EC decision to separate proceedings.

That distinction could matter considerably in the TMC case.

The Shiv Sena and NCP rebels who ultimately secured the original party identities had substantial support among sitting legislators. The TMC's internal arithmetic, however, has to be examined on its own terms.

The 2026 assembly election setback changed the party's internal arithmetic sharply. Its tally fell from 215 of 294 seats in 2021 to 80, and within weeks, 58 MLAs backed expelled leader Ritabrata Banerjee as their legislature party leader. He was subsequently recognised as leader of the opposition, while the rebel camp rejected Mamata's nominee, Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay.

The revolt then spread to Parliament, with 20 Lok Sabha MPs led by Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar joining the NCPI and backing the BJP-led NDA.

The TMC challenged their move before the Lok Sabha speaker and sought their disqualification. What began as a post-election leadership challenge had thus expanded into a contest over control of the party's legislative and parliamentary wings.

Mamata Banerjee, however, remains the founder and central political figure of the organisation, and her camp's claim is not based only on her position as party leader but also on its organisational and electoral support.

The 'new' Mamata party

The names allotted on Friday were revealing because neither faction chose to abandon the Trinamool identity. Mamata's camp was given 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress', while the rival Arup Roy camp became 'Democratic Trinamool Congress'. Both were, in different ways, laying claim to continuity with the party Mamata Banerjee founded on January 1, 1998.

The distinction lies in the source of legitimacy each side is emphasising.

The rebels' use of 'Democratic' fits their argument that the TMC's organisational functioning should be more representative and less centred around one leader. Mamata's faction, meanwhile, has effectively put the founder's name where the old party identity used to be, making 'Mamata' part of its temporary electoral brand. That is particularly striking for a party whose political identity has been inseparable from its founder for almost three decades.

They had said beforehand, 'naam bhi rakhne doonga, nishaan bhi nahi rakhne doonga' (Neither let you keep the name nor the symbol). Who are these people? They are in power today; they might not be in power tomorrow. They should understand their limitations. Mamata Banerjee

The football-player symbol allotted to Mamata's faction also carries its own political resonance in Bengal. Football has long had a deep cultural presence in the state, but there is also a direct connection to the TMC's campaign vocabulary: 'Khela Hobe', the slogan that became a defining part of Mamata's 2021 assembly campaign against the BJP.

The symbol does not automatically recreate that campaign, but it gives the Mamata faction a ready-made visual association at a time when it has lost the party symbol voters have known for nearly three decades.

The test, however, has now changed in a rather dramatic way for the Mamata faction.

Nandigram changes the bypoll test

Mamata faction's candidate, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew her nomination from the Nandigram contest altogether, a day before the deadline. Her withdrawal came minutes after she met West Bengal chief minister and BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari, although the circumstances surrounding the meeting and her decision remain a matter of political speculation.

Mamata Banerjee later announced in a press conference that her party will now back the Congress candidate in Nandigram, and mentioned that the decision was taken "for the greater interest of the nation" and to strengthen the INDIA bloc.

"Rahul Gandhi rang me up yesterday, Arvind Kejriwal also expressed solidarity; we will all fight together against BJP. We will support Congress in the Nandigram bypoll to strengthen the INDIA bloc," Mamata said.

The Congress candidate, however, was also arrested by the cops late in the evening in a land-grab case.

That makes the October 6 bypolls a very different test from the one that appeared possible 24 hours earlier. The Mamata faction will now not be testing its new 'football-player' identity in Nandigram, but instead, ask its supporters to transfer their support to a Congress candidate, even as the rival TMC faction contests the seat under its own new identity.

The political significance is difficult to miss. At precisely the moment when the EC has stripped Mamata's faction of the old TMC name and symbol and given it a new identity, the faction is now out of a direct fight in Nandigram, a constituency that carries an unusually strong personal history for both Mamata and Suvendu Adhikari.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Nandigram was where Mamata lost to Adhikari in the 2021 assembly election, after making the constituency the centrepiece of her campaign.

Adhikari, who had moved from the TMC to the BJP before that election, defeated her by a narrow margin in a contest that became one of the defining episodes of Bengal politics. He subsequently retained Nandigram while also winning Bhowanipore, which he vacated to retain Nandigram, necessitating the October 6 bypoll.

The EC may eventually decide who owns the TMC name and symbol, but the October 6 bypolls will offer the first test of how much of the old Trinamool identity survives without 'flowers and grass'. In Rejinagar, the football player and envelope will face each other directly; in Nandigram, Mamata's decision to back Congress will test whether her political support can travel even when her own new party name and symbol are not on the ballot.

World.title: Southern States urged to tap horticulture, export potential
World.content:
Union Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Friday called for Centre-State cooperation and region-specific planning to address the challenges confronting agriculture and improve farmers’ incomes.

Addressing the Southern States Regional Agriculture Conference here, Mr. Chouhan said agricultural policies and plans had to take into account differences in agro-climatic conditions, soil, water availability and cropping patterns across States.

“Nation First” was the guiding principle of the Centre and it did not approach agricultural issues based on which political party was in power in a State, he said. The conference discussed the impact of El Niño, crop diversification and preparations for the upcoming Rabi season.

Mr. Chouhan said the deliberations should result in tangible improvements in farmers’ lives, strengthen food security, create employment opportunities and contribute to economic growth.

The Minister said food security, farmers’ livelihoods and nutrition security were the three key objectives of agricultural policy. With a population of more than 140 crore, India could not afford to depend on other countries for its food requirements, he said.

At the same time, the farmer who feeds the country should have a secure and prosperous livelihood, making an increase in farm incomes a key priority. Ensuring access to nutritious food, rather than food alone, was equally important, he said.

Emphasising the continuing importance of agriculture amid rapid technological advances, Mr. Chouhan said artificial intelligence, machine learning and robotics would transform several sectors, but agriculture would remain indispensable.

Mr. Chouhan said a single agricultural plan could not adequately address the requirements of the entire country because of regional variations. The Rabi conference had consequently been expanded to two days to provide States greater opportunity to present their concerns and suggestions.

He said the challenges faced by Jammu and Kashmir, Gujarat and the northeastern States were different from those confronting Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Regional conferences would help formulate solutions suited to local conditions, he said.

The Minister urged States to study successful agricultural practices adopted elsewhere and adapt them to their own conditions. The Centre would extend support, while land and farmers remained primarily within the States’ domain, he said.

Mr. Chouhan urged States to review outdated laws, rules and procedures that could be hampering farmers and citizens. “Rules are meant for people; people are not meant for rules,” he said, adding that States should communicate to the Centre any issues requiring changes at the Union government level.

The Minister highlighted the potential of southern India in horticulture, particularly in spices, coffee, cashew, cocoa and coconut. He said coconut exports had increased from ₹4,349 crore to ₹7,038 crore in a year, a growth of 62%.

He said a new coconut promotion scheme announced in the Union Budget would soon become operational and urged southern States to prepare to maximise its benefits for farmers.

Mr. Chouhan said the Free Trade Agreements entered into by India had opened opportunities for agricultural exports. States should study international demand and encourage farmers to produce crops that met global quality standards, he said.

He called for adoption of international standards across the agricultural value chain so that farmers could benefit from access to global markets.

The Southern Regional Agriculture Conference brought together representatives of the Centre, southern States and Union Territories, agricultural experts, ICAR institutions, progressive farmers and other stakeholders to discuss region-specific priorities and strengthen coordination for sustainable and resilient agriculture.

World.title: Interests of a political party being served, says Mamata after losing TMC name and symbol; vows to fight back
World.content:
Former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Friday (September 18, 2026) said that she will fight and emerge stronger following the loss of the Trinamool Congress party name and symbol ahead of the byelections in the State.

The interests of a political party are being served, Ms. Banerjee said, addressing a press conference a day after the Election Commission of India (ECI) froze the symbol of “grass and twin flowers” along with the name ‘All India Trinamool Congress (AITC)’.

“Today is a black day in the history of democracy. Which is unfortunate, unconstitutional, anti-democratic, politically biased. The interests of a political party are being served,” she said.

The Commission on September 17 barred both factions, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction and the Ritabrata Banerjee-led faction of the party, from using the party symbol and name in the coming Assembly bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar in West Bengal scheduled on October 6.

Ms. Banerjee trained her guns on the poll body, saying that a “fake” SIR (Special Intensive Revision) was orchestrated followed by “not so clean” elections. “I do not respect the individual. He works for the BJP. He has done fake SIR, fake votes. CRPF has done the counting. He has thrown out the counting agent. He has hijacked the whole thing,” the Chairperson of Mamata All India Trinamool Congress said.

The ECI has allocated the name ‘Mamata All India Trinamool Congress’ to Ms. Banerjee’s faction with the symbol of a “football player” for the upcoming bypolls.

“We have temporarily submitted alternative names and symbol preferences only because the byelection process is already underway. This does not mean that we accept what has happened. We will return to our original symbol,” she said.

Ms. Banerjee also targeted the Ritabrata Banerjee-led faction of the party, which has been allocated the name ‘Democratic Trinamool Congress’, and said that they have betrayed their mother which was the name of the party and the symbol.

“If anyone really respected the Trinamool Congress, they would not insult its mother like this by snatching away the symbol and make it an orphan. Taking away the symbol shows that they never loved Trinamool,” she said.

Ms. Banerjee had founded the party in 1998 and herself had designed the symbol. During the press conference, she said that the party was set up after a long struggle and the party was 29 years old when the symbol and name was snatched away from her.

Meanwhile, leaders of the Ritabrata Banerjee-led faction said that they saved Trinamool symbol from disgrace. “This is a temporary decision for the bypoll. Grass and twin flower symbol will remain be with us. We have saved this symbol from disgrace. We have accepted what ECI directed us. We have faith in the agency,” said the Opposition Chief Whip Akhruzamman, who is key member of the faction.

Senior Bharatiya Janata Party leaders including Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and State party president Samik Bhattacharya said that it was divine intervention that Mamata Banerjee has lost her party’s symbol and name.

“This was a decision by the Election Commission. She was unable to keep her party together, BJP does not have any direct role in this. In the coming days no matter who survives, these people (Trinamool) will not survive because whoever becomes boastful will face consequences from God,” Mr. Adhikari said.

The bypolls for Nandigram and Rejinagar are scheduled on October 6.

World.title: Discussions over long-term growth strategy for ASR district
World.content:
A stakeholder consultation on the long-term growth strategy for Alluri Sitarama Raju (ASR) district was held on Thursday to deliberate on translating the recommendations of the ‘District as Fulcrum of Growth’ study into an actionable, place-based development framework for the district.

The consultation was attended by District Collector T. Nishanthi, Member, NITI Aayog, Balasubramanian, senior officials from various Union Government Ministries; district-level officials; and the IIM Visakhapatnam team.

The study was undertaken by IIM Visakhapatnam with the support of NITI Aayog and provides an evidence-based assessment of the development constraints, opportunities and potential growth pathways specific to ASR district.

The deliberations examined the distinctive development context of ASR District, including its tribal demographic profile, difficult Eastern Ghats terrain, dispersed habitations and ecological sensitivity.

The concept of ‘Terrain Penalty’, referring to the additional cost and operational challenges involved in delivering infrastructure, public services and economic opportunities across scattered and hilly habitations, was discussed as an important consideration for district-level planning. A key area of discussion was the proposed Growth Hub-and-Spoke Model, with Paderu as the principal growth hub, supported by secondary growth hubs at mandal and cluster levels and connected to remote habitations through last-mile physical and digital infrastructure.

The consultation discussed strengthening agricultural value chains through Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), post-harvest infrastructure, processing and storage, quality certification, market linkages and branding.

For the forest economy, discussions focused on increasing tribal participation and local value retention through decentralised GCC collection centres, primary processing, grading, price discovery, packaging and cooperative enterprise models.

Localised skill development pathways for tribal youth were also discussed, with potential linkages to emerging opportunities in coffee and food processing, Non-Timber Forest Produce (NTFP) value addition, eco-tourism, renewable energy, digital services and agri-technology.

The proposed development of 17 Model Panchayats under the Viksit Panchayat framework as demonstration sites for participatory planning, convergence of government schemes, livelihoods and digital governance was also discussed. The consultations considered developing practical models at these locations that could subsequently be adapted and replicated across other parts of the district.

In tourism, the consultation emphasised the importance of measuring outcomes beyond visitor numbers, including visitor-days, local expenditure retention, local employment and enterprise turnover. The approach seeks to strengthen local participation and improve the retention of tourism-generated economic value within the district.

Ms Nishanthi said that as a follow-up to the consultation, the District Administration will compile and examine the inputs and recommendations discussed during the meeting and coordinate with NITI Aayog, IIM Visakhapatnam, Union Government Ministries and concerned State Government departments for further technical examination. She also added that the identified development priorities and proposed interventions will be examined for their feasibility, institutional responsibilities, convergence requirements and measurable outcomes. Sector-wise inputs will be consolidated to support the preparation of an actionable development roadmap for the district.

World.title: Telangana took pro-active measures to tackle El Nino, says Deputy CM
World.content:
HYDERABAD

Deputy Chief Minister M. Bhatti Vikramarka on Friday stated that El Nino phenomenon had impacted Telangana in the form of deficient rainfall, reduced inflows into reservoirs, pressure on agriculture, and an increase in the electricity demand.

Anticipating the severity of the situation well in advance, the government began taking precautionary measures from April itself in coordination with various departments, he explained in the Assembly during a short discussion on the effect on El Nino and remedial measures. He stated that the rainfall deficit was 12% in June, 1% in July and a significant 38% in August.

Against the normal rainfall of 640 mm till September 18, Telangana had recorded only 543 mm, he noted. He pointed out that average rainfall figures alone do not fully reflect the severity of the situation as rainfall at the right time and at appropriate intervals was crucial for crops. One or two days of heavy rainfall cannot completely offset the impact of prolonged dry conditions that existed earlier, he explained.

About its impact on agriculture, he said the area under Kharif cultivation this year stood at 123.74 lakh acres against 139.29 lakh acres last year. Paddy cultivation had declined by around 18%, he said.

Citing the 15-minute interval data from TG-Transco, he stated that the combined load of major lift irrigation schemes was repeatedly recorded between 1,100 MW and 1,500 MW during the first half of August and reached nearly 1,600 MW on some occasions, while the load was generally between 250 MW and 450 MW during the period. On September 9, the State recorded the highest peak load of 19,453 MW.

Reduced rainfall also resulted in lower inflows into reservoirs, causing a significant decline in hydropower generation. Hydel generation fell to 422 MW this year, compared to 1,940 MW during the same period last year, the Deputy Chief Minister stated. Power purchase bids in the Day-Ahead Market of the energy exchange had increased by 61.7%, while the average energy price increased by 22%, he noted.

On wage employment, he said From April to June, an average of 12 lakh persons per day attended employment guarantee works and from July onwards, around 2 lakh persons per day were seeking employment during the lean agricultural period. During 2026–27, 7.3 crore person-days of employment were generated so far providing work to 31.5 lakh persons belonging to 21 lakh families and wages amounting to ₹2,100.53 crore were paid.

Ministers D. Seethakka, Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy, Ponnam Prabhakar, D. Sridhar Babu, members Ch. Vijayaramana Rao, J. Anirudh Reddy, Ch. Vamshi Krishna, B. Murali Naik, Adi Srinivas, B. Ilaiah and T. Rammohan Reddy (all Congress), A. Maheshwar Reddy, Payal Shankar, P. Harish Babu and P. Rakesh Reddy (all BJP), Kausar Mohiuddin (AIMIM) and K. Sambasiva Rao (CPI) participated in the discussion.

World.title: Online radicalisation case: NIA files chargesheet against 9 accused
World.content:
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Friday filed a chargesheet against nine accused in connection with an online radicalisation case.

The accused, identified as Mohammad Rehmatullah Shariff, Mohammed Danish, Mirza Sohail Baig, Lucky Ahmad, Jishan Abdul Majid, Mir Ashif Ali, Abdul Salaam, Sharuk Khan and Shaikh Faiz ur Rehman, had motivated and radicalised gullible youth to join violent terrorist activities, and also planned and prepared for making explosives and undertaking weapon training, according to the investigation.

A case was initially registered on March 26 earlier this year at Vijayawada II Town police station of the NTR Commissionerate. So far, 11 accused have arrested and a minor has been detained.

According to an NIA release, investigation has established that the accused, who are members and supporters of the proscribed terrorist organisation IS, entered into a larger conspiracy to support the activities of IS, primarily through social media platforms like Instagram, with the intention of establishing a caliphate in India through violent Jihad, thereby disrupting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of India.

Further investigation in the case against the remaining accused and other suspects is under way.

World.title: South African High Commission official visits Andhra University
World.content:
Sedula Mashudubele Mamabolo, Counsellor (Bilateral Relations), South African High Commission, New Delhi, visited Andhra University on Friday to discuss educational opportunities for South African students and academic engagement between the university and South Africa.

Mr. Mamabolo held discussions with Dean, International Affairs, S. Paul Douglas, and Director, Centre for Distance and Online Education, D.A. Naidu, on opportunities for South African students to pursue higher education through the university’s online and distance education programmes.

The discussions covered institutional linkages, student mobility and outreach to learners in South Africa. Mr. Mamabolo also interacted with South African students at the university to understand their academic experiences, opportunities and challenges.

He later met Andhra University Registrar Rambabu, who welcomed and felicitated him. Mr. Douglas said the university was keen to strengthen international partnerships and expand opportunities for overseas learners.

World.title: AU distance education admission deadline extended
World.content:
Andhra University has extended the deadline for admissions to its Centre for Distance and Online Education (CDOE) programmes to October 13, according to CDOE Director D.A. Naidu. The extension, in accordance with the instructions of the University Grants Commission-Distance Education Bureau (UGC-DEB), applies to Open and Distance Learning (ODL) offline programmes and Online Learning (OL) programmes for the July-August 2026 academic session.

Students seeking admission to the programmes have been advised to submit their applications by October 13. Applications for ODL (offline) programmes can be made through the website www.andhrauniversity-sde.com, while applications for online programmes can be submitted through the website www.andhrauniversity.edu.in.

World.title: BioMed Bharat 2026: MP calls upon youth to drive MedTech innovation
World.content:
Member of Parliament and GITAM president M. Sribharat called for greater collaboration among medicine, engineering, management and natural sciences to develop healthcare solutions at BioMed Bharat 2026, a two-day national Biomedical Device Innovation Hackathon hosted by GITAM Deemed to be University.

Mr. Sribharat said hackathons should be a starting point for developing solutions to real-world healthcare challenges and urged students and academic institutions to move beyond prototypes towards execution-ready solutions. He also highlighted the Andhra Pradesh Med Tech Zone (AMTZ) in Visakhapatnam as a major medical-device manufacturing cluster.

GITAM Institute of Medical Sciences and Research (GIMSR) Pro Vice-Chancellor Gitanjali Batmanabane urged participants to use artificial intelligence, robotics and 3D printing to develop affordable medical devices. She said 22 greenfield projects had been commissioned under the Production Linked Incentive scheme.

Progenics Laboratories & Aktachem Biotech Pvt. Ltd. managing director S. Venkata Prasad said medical-device exports reached $4.1 billion in 2024-25. Student teams competed for ₹4.5 lakh in prizes.

World.title: 15 cops among 21 martyred in blast at Kohat Police Lines, more than 80 injured
World.content:
PESHAWAR: At least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred on Friday when an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines, followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities, according to senior police and district health officials.

District Health Officer Dr Nasir Hassan Afridi confirmed the toll to Dawn, adding that more than 100 people were injured, with three in critical condition.

According to officials, SP Traffic Akbar Shinwari and Dr Israel Orakzai, head of the children’s department at DHQ KDA Kohat, were among those martyred in the attack.

According to police, at least one attacker was holed up inside the compound and a clearance operation was underway.

Meanwhile, the CTD said the Additional IG CTD reached the site of the Kohat attack. An exchange of fire between CTD personnel and the terrorist was ongoing, the department said, adding that the AIG had entered the site himself to take part in the operation and lead the personnel.

Later in the evening, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed visited the police lines as the clearance operation continued. According to a statement, the IGP met GOC Kohat, the regional police officer, the district police officer Kohat and other officers and personnel present at the site.

The attack

According to IG Hameed and police statements, the attack began when a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED) detonated at the boundary wall near the mosque inside the Kohat Police Lines.

At least seven attackers then breached the compound and headed towards the CTD and Special Branch buildings. Six attackers, including a suicide bomber, were killed by law enforcers, according to a police statement.

At least one attacker was subsequently cornered, prompting police personnel to launch a clearance operation. At around 3:30pm, police said the operation was “in its final stages”.

“The operation will continue until the complete elimination of Fitna-ul-Khawarij,” the IG was quoted as saying, adding that the police’s morale remained high.

Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

Earlier, television footage from the scene showed citizens gathered beside a building with a collapsed wall, digging through the rubble and helping the injured. The blast caused extensive damage to the mosque.

The attack was claimed by the Hafiz Gul Bahadur-led Ittehadul Mujahideen.

Separately, KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi sought a detailed report on the incident, saying the targeting of innocent citizens was “deeply regrettable and unacceptable,” as per a statement issued by his office.

Residents gather on a street leading to a police facility, where ambulances are parked following a suicide attack in Kohat on September 18. — Reuters

He directed authorities to ensure immediate treatment for the injured. “The nation’s morale cannot be dampened by cowardly acts of terrorism,” he was quoted as saying.

The funeral prayers for 15 police personnel martyred in the Police Lines blast were offered in Kohat later in the evening, after which their bodies were transported to their native districts of Kohat, Karak, Lakki Marwat, Bannu and Mardan in Rescue 1122 ambulances.

In 2010, 20 people, mostly the relatives of policemen, were killed and more than 90 injured in a remote-controlled bomb blast inside a police colony located just behind the Kohat Police Lines.

Condemnations pour in

President Asif Ali Zardari, condemning the incident, vowed that the complete elimination of foreign-sponsored terrorists was “essential for national security”.

President Zardari wished the injured a swift recovery.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif sought a report on the blast from the concerned authorities. He also directed authorities to expedite relief operations, Radio Pakistan reported.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also condemned the blast, praying for the recovery of the injured.

“The entire nation stands with the security forces to eradicate terrorism,” he said in a statement.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said in his condemnation that terrorists’ “cowardly acts cannot weaken the nation’s resolve”.

A statement posted on his ministry’s X account said Naqvi expressed grief over the loss of lives in the attack and extended condolence to the bereaved.

“The nation is standing with the families of the martyrs in this moment of grief,” he was quoted as saying.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi also strongly condemned the suicide attack in Kohat and expressed his condolences over the deaths of police personnel and civilians.

In a video message, he said the people of KP had sacrificed more than 80,000 lives for Pakistan and continued to bear the brunt of the fight against terrorism.

“Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is Pakistan’s frontline province in the war against terrorism,” he said, adding that peace in Islamabad and the rest of the country was due to the sacrifices made by the people of the province.

He also criticised those who, he said, labelled the people of KP as terrorists, saying such remarks reopened their wounds and disrespected their martyrs.

Referring to comments by the chief minister of another province, Afridi said it was regrettable to suggest that the threat to Pakistan came from its other provinces rather than India. He said KP and the other provinces were patriotic and had made sacrifices for the country.

“Pakistan is our country, and we will not allow any conspiracy to succeed,” he said, adding that efforts to create division, prejudice and hatred among the people would be thwarted.

United Kingdom’s High Commissioner in Pakistan said she was “appalled by the horrific attack” in Kohat.

“Nobody should face violence in a place of worship“,” she said, adding that her thoughts were with those injured and those who lost loved ones in the attack.

China’s embassy in Pakistan said it was “deeply saddened” by the terrorist attack. It condemned the attack and added that it extends “deepest condolences to the deceased victims and sincere sympathies to the breaved families”.

Russia’s embassy in Pakistan also strongly condemned the attack.

“This terrible tragedy, which claimed numerous lives, once again underscores the need for concerted efforts to combat terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. We hope that those responsible for this heinous act will be identified and brought to justice.”

The mission added that their hearts go out to the families and friends of the victims. “We wish a speedy recovery to all those injured.”

World.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs1.65 per litre, HSD by Rs0.88 per litre
World.content:
The government on Friday reduced the price of petrol by Rs1.65 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs0.88 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs389.14 per litre while HSD will cost Rs424.04 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable from Sept 19 (Saturday) to Sept 21 (Monday).

According to Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA), the increase is primarily linked to higher petrol and diesel prices in the international market.

The regulator said the prices were revised based on international market rates, premiums and other relevant factors.

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

The government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices, including requiring markets to close by 9pm and cutting fuel allocations for official vehicles by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

A statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said owners of two- and three-wheelers would receive relief of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while owners of vehicles up to 800cc would receive the same relief on a monthly quota of 30 litres.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Govt to stop anyone marching on Islamabad 'in every possible way', says Naqvi
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said on Friday that the government would stop anyone from marching towards the federal capital “in every possible way” and file contempt of court proceedings against those who violated a recent Islamabad High Court (IHC) decision.

He was addressing a press conference in Islamabad alongside other officials.

The interior minister’s remarks came in the wake of PTI’s call for a nationwide protest , including in Islamabad, on September 27 to demand the release of party founder Imran Khan and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.

Last week, the administrations of the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad started preparations to counter the PTI’s announced countrywide protest, including a request for detention of activists, arranging containers, seeking additional personnel and procuring anti-riot gear.

At the outset of his press conference on Friday, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said a detailed meeting had been held to discuss the upcoming protest call and the law and order situation. Officials from all provinces and federal law enforcement agencies had also attended the meeting.

“In light of the detailed IHC judgment, there is no possibility of ravaging the federal capital or any other province,” he said.

The minister said that if anyone took to the streets, the government would first pursue legal action by filing a contempt petition against them for violating the IHC order.

At the same time, he said, “We will stop the marchers in every possible way.” All law enforcement agencies had been informed of the decision “with all clarity”, Naqvi added.

He said weapons had been used and losses suffered in protests in the past.

“This time, we are communicating very clear rules of engagement to our law enforcement agencies. They will not remain silent if a bullet is fired at them,” he said.

He urged the protesting party’s leadership to hold demonstrations in their respective provinces and cities. “Plans for locking down the capital or charging into another province will never be allowed,” he said.

“It is our responsibility to stop this protest to ensure the protection of the lives and property of the capital’s residents,” the interior minister said.

The interior minister drew a distinction between a political protest aimed at pursuing political interests and a violent campaign involving people armed with weapons.

“There is complete clarity. The organisers of this march will be held accountable if even a single life is lost,” he said.

Naqvi said there were still some “sensible” voices within the opposition and hoped they would reconsider their decision. “There is only loss in it, no sort of gain at all,” he added.

He reiterated that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had repeatedly invited the opposition from the floor of parliament to hold talks on all issues. “If you want to resolve matters through violent mobs, we are ready for it,” he said.

The interior minister reaffirmed that the government had finalised its preparations and all law enforcement agencies were ready.

“We will not allow people to spread turbulence as happened in the past,” he said.

In a detailed judgment issued today, the IHC ruled that any activity resulting in infringement of citizens’ fundamental rights amounts to a violation of the Constitution.

It warned that public office holders responsible for such violations would also be deemed to have breached their oath of office.

The court also held that the right to peaceful assembly could not be exercised in a manner that infringed the fundamental rights of other citizens.

Kohat attack

Commenting on the attack in Kohat, Naqvi said security agencies had been fighting terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

“We have to focus on this, rather than making strategies for mobilising masses, arranging transport and collecting money,” he said.

“After such incidents, it doesn’t suit you to call for long marches and, on the other hand, lift the dead bodies of martyrs,” he added.

He further said the KP chief minister and his cabinet should work towards eradicating terrorism with the same spirit with which they were carrying out campaigns for long marches.

Earlier today, at least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred when an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines. More than 80 people were injured, according to the officials.

The incident was followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities, according to senior police and district health officials.

World.title: IHC rules infringement of fundamental rights breaches Constitution ahead of PTI’s Sept 27 protest
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has ruled that any activity resulting in infringement of citizens’ fundamental rights amounts to a violation of the Constitution, warning that public office holders responsible for such violations would also be deemed to have breached their oath of office.

The ruling came in a detailed 37-page judgment on a petition concerning the proposed nationwide PTI protest towards Islamabad on September 27, 2026. PTI had announced the march to demand release of party founder Imran Khan and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.

A citizen, Waqas Ahmed, had challenged the planned move on the grounds that the protest could disrupt routine life, traffic and business activities in the federal capital.

A three-member bench headed by Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and comprising Justice Muhammad Asif and Justice Muhammad Azam Khan issued the judgment.

The bench had announced its short order on September 14 after hearing Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Awan, Additional Attorney General Amir Rehman, the advocate generals of the four provinces and Islamabad, and counsel for the petitioner, Barrister Akhter Cheena.

The court described the case as requiring an “unusual degree of constitutional balance” between the right of political parties and citizens to assemble peacefully and express dissent, and the rights of other citizens to life, liberty, dignity, free movement, trade, business, property, and access to hospitals, educational institutions, courts and workplaces.

“The question is not whether a political party is entitled to protest. It plainly is, subject always to the Constitution and law,” the judgment observed.

The court held that the right to peaceful assembly could not be exercised in a manner that infringed the fundamental rights of other citizens.

A key objection raised by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa advocate general concerned the territorial jurisdiction of the IHC over provincial authorities functioning outside Islamabad.

Rejecting the objection, the court held that Article 199(1)(c) empowered a high court to issue directions where a governmental power or function was being exercised “in, or in relation to” territory within its jurisdiction.

The court clarified, however, that the provision did not confer general supervisory jurisdiction over another province. A high court could issue directions to an authority outside its territorial seat where the governmental function had a direct and proximate legal relation with territory within its jurisdiction and intervention was necessary to protect fundamental rights there.

The bench also observed that where executive action or inaction was likely to infringe the fundamental rights of citizens within Islamabad, the court was under a “bounden duty” to assume jurisdiction under Article 199(1)(c).

The court also rejected the objection that the petition was not maintainable because KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had not been impleaded as a respondent. It noted that the Advocate General KP was representing both the provincial government and the chief minister.

The court further rejected the argument that the petitioner had an adequate alternate remedy under the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act, 2024.

It noted that no application had, admittedly, been filed under Section 3 of the Act and observed that its provisions had not been adhered to by the KP chief minister and others who had announced their intention to march towards Islamabad.

The judgment extensively referred to the Supreme Court’s decision in the Faizabad sit-in case, observing that the constitutional right to assemble and protest was protected but remained subject to restrictions where its exercise infringed the fundamental rights of others.

The IHC also referred to the Supreme Court judgment concerning the PTI march of May 25, 2022, noting that assurances regarding a peaceful rally and non-obstruction of the Srinagar Highway had not been honoured.

The judgment referred to damage to public and private property, fires in the Blue Area greenbelt, injuries to police personnel and the subsequent invocation of Article 245 to call in the armed forces in aid of civil power.

The court also cited its November 21, 2024 order directing that no protest, rally or sit-in be allowed in violation of the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act. It observed that the order had also been flouted.

During the proceedings, the court allowed the Islamabad deputy commissioner/district magistrate to place electronic material on record. Video clips of the 2022 and 2024 protests were played before the bench, which described the conduct shown in the footage as “highly disturbing and reflective of violence and aggression”.

The court noted that PTI was in power in KP during both episodes and observed that provincial government resources had been used in pursuit of political objectives.

Regarding the proposed September 27 march, the court held that the petitioner’s apprehension was not merely speculative. It noted that the date and destination of the proposed gathering were known and that statements attributed to the KP chief minister indicated that the date was firm and that he intended to lead the march.

While disposing of the petition, the court directed that no political party, political leader, provincial government or public office holder could lawfully occupy roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas, buildings or similar public places within, or leading to or from, Islamabad in a manner that obstructed free movement or hindered trade, business, professions or access to medical and educational facilities.

The provincial governments and chief ministers were directed to ensure that no government resources, public funds, officials, vehicles, machinery or equipment were used directly or indirectly to facilitate any march, rally or procession towards Islamabad.

They were also directed to ensure that no public servant was compelled, coerced or induced to participate in such activities.

The chief secretaries, police chiefs, federal interior secretary, chief commissioner and IG Islamabad were ordered to issue instructions prohibiting officials from complying with orders requiring them to facilitate such marches.

Officials facing coercion were directed to report the matter to the relevant authorities, while helplines or other communication mechanisms were ordered to be established for this purpose.

The court further directed the authorities to take departmental action against officials who violated the directions.

In a significant finding, the court held that any person whose activity resulted in a violation of the fundamental rights of citizens in Islamabad would be deemed to have violated the Constitution and would be liable for consequences under the law.

It further declared that any public office holder whose activity resulted in a violation of citizens’ fundamental rights would be deemed to have violated both the Constitution and his or her oath of office.

World.title: JI chief says govt could save up to Rs4 trillion if it adopts party’s proposed fiscal reforms
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman on Friday said the party’s protest movement aimed to press the government for immediate economic relief, asserting that the national exchequer could save between Rs3 trillion and Rs4 trillion if the authorities adopted the party’s proposed fiscal reforms.

Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, the JI chief voiced sharp criticism of rising fuel costs and heavy taxation, as well as what he characterised as superficial relief packages that failed to address the core burdens facing the public.

Rehman announced that a nationwide “super long march” towards the federal capital would commence on September 20.

He rejected the government’s argument that recent energy and fuel price hikes were strictly attributable to international market forces, saying the authorities were relying on aggressive levies to meet revenue targets rather than reducing state expenditure.

The JI chief noted that local fuel prices had risen significantly faster than those in neighbouring countries during recent regional tensions, disproportionately affecting lower- and middle-income households that rely heavily on smaller vehicles.

Calling for an end to guaranteed profit margins for oil marketing companies at the expense of consumers, Rehman reiterated the JI’s demands to abolish the petroleum levy, end non-productive capacity payments to independent power producers (IPPs) and regasification plants, and fix the price of petrol at Rs225 per litre.

Outlining key economic measures, the JI emir called for an immediate cut of three percentage points in the benchmark interest rate, pointing out that every one-percentage-point reduction would save the exchequer approximately Rs574 billion. He said the government must stop protecting commercial bank profits and instead work towards systematically eliminating interest from the national economy.

“The public’s support for the party’s movement is growing,” Rehman said, confirming ongoing dialogue and mutual political support with farmers’ alliances and PTI over their respective demonstrations.

“The September 20 demonstration will involve caravans travelling to Islamabad from across Sindh, Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, including a dedicated contingent travelling by train from Karachi,” he said.

Rehman assured the public that the self-funded march would not involve road blockades or cause unnecessary disruption to daily life, adding that its arrangements would not obstruct students appearing for the upcoming Medical and Dental College Admission Test (MDCAT).

While expressing readiness for immediate talks if the government presented actionable proposals, the JI leadership warned that stalling tactics would not be tolerated as public mobilisation intensified.

World.title: Lawyers’ body to boycott Islamabad court proceedings on Saturday in protest against Imaan, Hadi’s rearrest
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad Bar Association (IBA) has announced a boycott of court proceedings in the federal capital on Saturday (September 19) to protest the rearrest of human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, after the Supreme Court suspended their sentences and ordered their release on bail.

Imaan and Hadi were arrested late on Thursday in a second case after the SC ordered their release in a case pertaining to their posts on social media. The couple was sentenced to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in the case.

However, soon after their release on Thursday, Islamabad police personnel arrested the two outside Adiala jail in connection with another case and produced them before an anti-terrorism court, which sent them to jail on judicial remand.

The second case was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22, 2025 on a complaint by City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio. Imaan and her husband were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads and were named in the first information report (FIR).

The IBA expressed concern over the couple’s rearrest in a statement on Friday and announced that lawyers would not appear before any court in the capital on Sept 19 (Saturday).

The bar association said the arrest undermined the sanctity of judicial proceedings and amounted to a violation of fundamental rights and the rule of law.

It also expressed strong reservations over the practice of arresting individuals in connection with “unknown” FIRs. The IBA held that any attempt to circumvent or frustrate court orders was unacceptable.

It demanded the immediate release of Imaan and Hadi and called for complete details of the cases and circumstances surrounding their arrests to be made public.

The association vowed to take every possible measure to safeguard judicial independence, uphold the rule of law and protect fundamental human rights.

Amnesty International, HRCP demand immediate and unconditional release

Global rights watchdog Amnesty Inter­national condemned the arrest and held that the action demonstrated “authorities’ willingness to weaponise the legal system against critical voices”.

“Imaan and Hadi’s re-arrest dispels any pretence that the charges against them are anything other than a politically motivated attempt to punish them for their human rights work,” rights body’s South Asia director, Babu Ram Pant, said in a statement.

Pant held that charges were “not only absurd, but an insult to their lifelong commitment to human rights”.

The official called on the Pakistani authorities to release the couple immediately and “unconditionally, with no further charges to prolong their detention”.

“Imaan and Hadi should be free to meet their friends and family and to do the work they love – representing victims of human rights violations.”

Meanwhile, the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan, in a post on X, also demanded Imaan and Hadi’s release and withdrawal of all cases against them.

World.title: Karachi police claim to unearth international meth supply network, arrest two
World.content:
KARACHI: Police on Friday claimed to have unearthed an international narcotics network involved in the supply of ice — methamphetamine, also known as crystal meth — with the arrest of two of its members, including a woman.

Speaking at a press conference in Karachi, East Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) Dr Farrukh Ali said Landhi police, acting on a tip-off, had arrested two suspected members of the network.

The police also recovered 19.56 kilograms of meth from their possession, he added.

The DIG said the suspects were in contact with a notorious Afghan drug dealer, Sabir Afghan.

“The held suspects belonged to an Afghanistan-linked network of drug dealers who supplied narcotics in Karachi and other parts of the country,” DIG Dr Ali claimed.

He alleged that it was an organised network that supplied drugs from Afghanistan through different routes to Lahore and other parts of Punjab, from where they were subsequently distributed to other parts of the country, including Karachi.

DIG Dr Ali said the “international network” was essentially a family-based cartel whose linchpin was a woman named Mehwish, who lived in Lahore.

“Mehwish used to supply high-quality ice from Afghanistan, which was then distributed throughout the country,” he said, adding that the arrested woman, was Mehwish’s sister-in-law.

The woman’s husband supplied the ice, while the wife distributed it to customers, the senior official claimed.

“This family consists of working- or middle-class people. One member of the cartelwas recently arrested by the Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF),” he said.

He said further investigation was under way to obtain information from the suspects about their drug network and accomplices.

In a lighter vein, DIG Dr Ali said the family-based cartel could be dubbed “Pinky Two”, as it had also maintained the same level of secrecy as Anmol, alias Pinky, who is currently facing trial in Karachi.

Anmol was arrested in May in connection with two cases registered at the Garden police station pertaining to the possession of drugs and an unlicensed weapon. She had already been booked in multiple other criminal cases prior to her arrest.

The incident gained attention when a video of her being escorted to court without handcuffs went viral on social media.

Since her arrest, Anmol has been presented in court amid heavy police presence. During her court appearances, she has also alleged that she has been facing pressure from the police “to take names ” of politicians and other influential persons.

Earlier in the month, police also claimed to have recovered a huge quantity of ice and arrested eight suspects in an intelligence-based raid on a warehouse in Mehran Town in Korangi.

World.title: Supreme Court admonishes Sindh police over delays in filing FIRs
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court on Friday expressed strong displeasure over delays in the registration of first information reports (FIRs) in Sindh, cautioning police officials that they could face contempt proceedings over any future delays.

A two-judge SC bench, comprising Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar and Justice Salahuddin Panhwar, upheld the life sentence of a man convicted of a 2012 murder in Sindh’s Dadu district while hearing the jail petition of Ali Raza Siyal, who had challenged the Sindh High Court’s Aug 24, 2023, Circuit Bench at Larkana judgment upholding his sentence.

“We observe with dismay, once again, the consistent practice of delayed registration of FIRs in the province of Sindh,” Justice Salahuddin Panhwar observed in a seven-page judgment, adding that despite earlier directions — and even after the Sindh inspector general had appeared before the court — the practice showed no sign of abating.

In this case, the FIR was registered after a delay of more than three days. Although information had been furnished the same night, the judgment expressed regret and recalled that it had called these delays out in the 2026 Muhammad Bux case.
