World.id: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019025/The Chinese Dating App Promising Marriage — or Your Money Back
World.title: The Chinese Dating App Promising Marriage — or Your Money Back
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019025/The Chinese Dating App Promising Marriage — or Your Money Back
World.content:
A new Chinese dating app is betting that AI can do more than keep users chatting — it wagers it can see them married in three years or less.

If it fails, the team behind Liangpei — roughly “good match” in Chinese — promises to refund the user’s one-time fee of 2,000 yuan ($275). The guarantee comes as marriage rates fall in China, with only 6.76 million couples tying the knot in 2025, about half the number a decade earlier.

Launched this past July, Liangpei begins with a roughly 20-minute voice conversation with an AI matchmaker. Users answer 25 questions about their relationship history, marriage plans, and even whether they intend to buy property. The system then uses their answers to build a detailed profile, calculate compatibility scores, and recommend potential partners.

Once two people match, they can talk only until one decides to move on, a restriction the app’s developers say is intended to keep them focused on one relationship rather than constantly searching for alternatives.

“We want to get the users off the platform as soon as possible,” founder Zeng Xinxun told Sixth Tone.

Before launching Liangpei, the 32-year-old worked on AI search technology at Kimi, one of China’s best-known generative AI platforms. His 18-person team now uses similar technology to draw out information that basic dating-app tags such as age, occupation, and location cannot capture.

Approximately 91% of users who start Liangpei’s interview finish it, Zeng said, going on to create profiles averaging 516 Chinese characters, about four times as long as those on several major Chinese dating apps.

About one in 10 users has reached an exclusive one-on-one match, according to Zeng. Those conversations last more than 10 days on average and run to more than 200 messages.

“One-on-one allows both parties to invest more focus and effort into building a relationship,” Zeng said. “Even if it doesn’t work out, it’s a conclusion reached after genuine communication.”

So far, he said, Liangpei has more than 9,300 active users across 300 cities. Men account for 57% of users, and women 43%. The two largest age groups are 26 to 28 and 29 to 31.

China’s established dating and social platforms operate at a much larger scale. Tantan, one of the country’s oldest dating apps, had 10.7 million monthly active users in March 2025, while Soul draws large audiences with broader offerings that combine dating, social discovery, entertainment, and shared interests.

Liangpei also requires real-name registration, a marital status check, and live photo verification. The company has blocked 487 people found to be married, Zeng said. It also uses AI to watch for signs of fraud once conversations begin.

Wang, a Shanghai-based user who asked to be identified only by her surname for privacy reasons, has tried more than 10 dating apps. Liangpei was the first on which she was willing to answer so many questions.

“It has helped me understand myself better and clarified exactly what I’m looking for,” she said.

Within a week, Wang entered an exclusive one-on-one match. She said the format made online dating less exhausting and allowed her to focus on getting to know her counterpart. But with no other matches to turn to, the arrangement depended on that person keeping the conversation alive.

“Once matched, your slot is locked,” Wang said. “If the other person isn’t proactive, you’re left waiting with nowhere for the conversation to go.”

On Xiaohongshu, the lifestyle app also known as RedNote, Liangpei has drawn sharply mixed reactions. Some users described it as a welcome option for people anxious about finding a spouse, while others questioned whether treating marriage as a fixed target made dating too rigid.

Free users can send only one “like” a day, according to posts reviewed by Sixth Tone. The app also prominently displays compatibility scores, which some users said made them more reluctant to start conversations.

Despite the compatibility score, several users admitted they still ended up judging potential partners by appearance.

Three-year itch

Six years ago, Zeng said he became frustrated trying to meet someone online — a period that lasted a year. He wrote a lengthy profile, but few people seemed to read it, and even fewer replied.

“Profiles were too bare to spark interest,” he said. Zeng eventually expanded his own to around 2,000 Chinese characters, then came across a woman whose profile was just as detailed.

“We quickly went from strangers to a close connection,” Zeng said. By the time they met in person, he thought the relationship might go somewhere.

They are now married. And Liangpei uses that same outcome as its measure of success.

His team had considered a first date or the start of a relationship instead. Marriage, Zeng said, was different: “It’s legally verifiable and undisputed.”

The three-year cutoff came after his team interviewed 150 couples obtaining marriage licenses at a civil affairs bureau in the southern city of Shenzhen. More than 70% said they had married within three years of meeting, Zeng said.

Liangpei has been operating for only a few months, so none of its users have yet to reach that deadline. For now, the company is reviewing the data it does have, including whether higher compatibility scores are associated with more likes, replies, and longer conversations.

“For example, among 1,500 users in Shenzhen, the AI can directly rank the top 10 people most likely to succeed with you,” Zeng said. “You don’t have to browse everyone — just start with the highest scores.”

To address relationship anxiety, Liangpei offers an “icebreaker” feature that suggests questions when a conversation stalls. An “AI wingman” can also analyze an exchange and offer advice.

But the “AI wingman” will not compose replies. Zeng said someone who struggles with online banter might still make a good partner in person, but AI should only carry early exchanges far enough for both people to find out.

Du Shichao, an assistant professor of sociology at Shanghai’s Fudan University, said Liangpei’s focus on marriage could appeal to people who already know what they are looking for. He also saw value in matching people using more than surface-level information.

“It may not address everyone’s pain points, but it can at least solve problems for some people and offer them more choice,” Du said.

But he was more cautious about AI taking on a larger role in relationships.

“This ‘enhancement’ can easily slide into ‘replacement,’” Du said. “When this kind of use is taken to an extreme, people need to be wary of ceding their capacity for emotional connection to technology.”

Whatever help an AI assistant can provide online, he said, people still have to learn about each other in person. “Ultimately, people must rediscover each other and themselves through real-world interaction.”

Du said technology may help with some of the difficulties individuals face in meeting and communicating with partners, but it cannot address the forces shaping marriage more broadly, including demographics, economic pressure, and family expectations.

“It may benefit some, but won’t significantly change China’s marriage patterns,” he said.

Zeng is making a more modest claim. “We don’t need to serve everyone,” he said. “We can’t help those with particularly poor prospects, or those with unrealistic expectations. If the people in between can find success in Liangpei, that’s good enough.”

Whether they do will become clear in 2029, when Liangpei’s first users reach the end of its three-year guarantee.

Additional reporting: Xu Ruishuo; editor: Apurva.

World.content:
Here are today’s headlines – the latest news in the Philippines and around the world:

Graft complaints are now pending against members of the Villar family due to allegations related to PrimeWater Infrastructure Corporation. This, as confirmed by the Office of the Ombudsman.

At least three children are killed and six others wounded after a minor opened fire at Banga National High School in South Cotabato, as confirmed by Governor Reynaldo Tamayo Jr.

The Philippines sees a lower bullying rate in 2025 but it still has one of the highest rates among participating countries.

A Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources vessel sustains damage to its metal stanchions and supports, deck fixtures and equipment, and main railings, after being rammed by a China Coast Guard ship.

World.title: How watchdogs got sidelined again in 2027 House budget talks
World.content:
The People's Budget Coalition appeals to the House of Representatives to 'make CSO participation meaningful,' not 'tokenistic'

MANILA, Philippines – Civil society organizations (CSOs) flagged limited access and late notice in the House of Representatives’ deliberations on the proposed 2027 national budget.

“CSO participation in the House budget process has been repeatedly sidelined,” People’s Budget Coalition (PBC) co-coordinator Gybel Agregado said in an online briefing on Friday, September 18.

The PBC said the process fell short of the House committee on appropriations’ commitment to civil society participation, with watchdog groups given limited opportunities to engage in key budget discussions.

“Civil society felt left out of the budget process after being inbox-zoned and seen-zoned multiple times,” the PBC said.

Agregado shared that members of their coalition had sent questions related to the budget deliberations of government agencies to the House of Representatives, but they did not receive any response.

Agregado said CSOs taking part in the People’s Budget Review were given only three minutes each to speak during hearings on the final day of committee deliberations, which she said was not enough.

The PBC also cited instances when CSOs were given short notice of changes to the budget calendar.

The coalition acknowledged the efforts of the Congressional Policy and Budget Research Department to engage civil society, as well as the Senate committee on finance’s more direct engagement with CSOs.

But the PBC said technical consultations are not a substitute for direct participation in the House appropriations committee, where key decisions on the budget are made.

The coalition called on the House to directly involve CSOs in budget deliberations and amendments, reopen its accreditation process for civil society groups, and publish amendment and realignment documents promptly in machine-readable formats.

It also urged lawmakers to advance transparency measures such as the proposed CADENA act, which has little to no progress in the House of Representatives.

The PBC also appealed to the House of Representatives to “make CSO participation meaningful,” not “tokenistic.”

The issues raised this year were similar to those encountered by CSOs in 2025. Last year, civil society groups also flagged restricted access and late notices for budget deliberations.

– Rappler.com

World.title: For Aznar Shipping, going public means growth – and dodging third-gen curse
World.content:
'My main job is really to hand it over to the next gen,' the third-generation Aznar tells Rappler. 'Looking at the IPO process, the requirements, the standards that you are held to, it really coincided with my interest.'

As his family’s shipping legacy prepares to open itself up to the public, Kyle Alexander Aznar had an age-old curse on his mind.

“You know what they say, the third generation is the last generation,” the Aznar Shipping president and CEO told Rappler on Friday, September 18.

He was, of course, referring to the infamous adage that warns family fortunes rarely survives three generations. The first makes the money, second grows it, the third squanders what’s left. Gone, wasted, kaput.

The third-generation Aznar wasn’t about to let that happen. He was only 27 when he suddenly had to take over the family shipping business after his father died. Now 31 and at the helm, he sees one job as more important than simply making money.

“My main job is really to hand it over to the next gen,” Aznar told Rappler at the sidelines of his company’s H1 briefing. “We want our business to succeed — not just for my time. It’s really succeeding generations.”

His chosen way to keep the family ship afloat for another generation? Open it up to the public.

Aznar Shipping has filed for an initial public offering (IPO) that could see the Cebu-based company sell as many as one billion primary shares at an indicative price of up to P0.67 each, potentially raising P670 million in gross proceeds for the company. Another 100 million secondary shares could be sold through an overallotment option, bringing the total potential offer size to P737 million.

At this stage, everything still remains subject to book building and approval by the Securities and Exchange Commission and Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE). Aznar said the company is targeting a December listing, but stressed that he did not want to “jump the gun” on regulators.

A family business trying to grow up

Aznar is hardly the only old name sailing out of Cebu.

Cebu has long been one of the country’s biggest shipping hubs, producing generations of shipping families, from the Gothongs and Robles to the Cokaliongs and the Lims. The Aboitizes were once part of that club too, with Aboitiz Shipping eventually evolving into 2GO, now under the Sy family’s SM group. (READ: As Atlas Mining leaves by 2027, SMIC expects 2GO, renewables to fill gap)

But while many shipping businesses have remained private and closely held, Aznar sees public company governance as part of the antidote to the generational curse.

“Looking at the IPO process, the requirements, the standards that you are held to, it really coincided with my interest. That’s how I first started getting interested in it quite a few years ago,” he told Rappler.

The professionalization actually began before the IPO. Even before the company’s aspirations to go public, the shipping company already had independent directors sitting on its board. Aznar said he has been the only family member on the board for the past three years, surrounded instead by professionals whom he calls his mentors.

“I was just only 27 when I had to take over the company when my dad passed away,” he said. “I was humble enough to realize that I might not have all the answers, I might not always be right.”

That setup, he believes, has paid off.

FINANCIALS. Aznar Shipping chief financial officer Dary Aran shares the company’s H1 2026 financial results. Photo by Lance Spencer Yu/Rappler.

Aznar Shipping’s revenue jumped from P59.2 million in 2023 to P223.9 million in 2025, when it booked P51.7 million in net income. In just the first six months of 2026, revenue reached P210.9 million while net income hit P53.2 million, already topping the previous full year.

The company currently operates nine vessels across four principal Visayas corridors, with cargo and rolling vehicles accounting for about 86% of first-half revenue.

The company wants to use IPO proceeds primarily for fleet expansion, with plans for newer vessels and, farther down the road, its own dry-docking facility. Aznar also said his company is not specifically hunting the customers of rivals.

“We’re not really eyeing specific players,” he told Rappler. “We’re following the market. We’re looking at complementary routes. We’re following our customers.”

Rough waters for an IPO?

If Aznar wants to test whether investors believe the family business can survive another generation, he’s choosing a challenging time to do it.

Even before getting to the stock market, the shipping industry is contending with elevated fuel prices. Aznar said fuel is the company’s biggest operating cost, although its move toward larger vessels has helped protect margins because capacity has increased much faster than operating expenses. (READ: DOE sees ‘no signs’ oil prices will fall as excise tax relief goes on table)

“Our new vessel could probably carry three or four times the load of our previous one. But the operating cost is more or less the same,” he said. “That’s how we’ve kept our rates affordable. That’s how we’ve protected our margins as well.”

So far, Aznar said demand has held up despite the broader economic uncertainty. “Our numbers are good,” he said. “The demand is there. The volume is there. And I believe it’s the right time to expand.”

But the bigger uncertainty may be whether investors will be equally ready.

The PSE index remains below the 6,000 level amid worries over slow economic growth and broader market uncertainty, well below the roughly 7,800 level where it ended 2019 before the pandemic.

Then there’s the very large elephant potentially barging into the stock exchange just weeks ahead of Aznar: GCash.

Mynt, the operator of GCash, is targeting an October 20 listing for an IPO worth as much as P92.3 billion, dwarfing Aznar’s planned offering. Would there still be enough liquidity left in the market after the biggest IPO in Philippine history when Aznar comes knocking in December?

The young shipowner, for his part, offered an appropriately maritime answer to the uncertainty.

“Market conditions, they’re out of our control. They’re just like the sea. You can’t always hope for calm waters,” he said. “What you can do is really learn to sail in rough conditions.” – Rappler.com

World.title: FACT CHECK: No evidence Romualdez has stage 4 cancer
World.content:
The lawmaker is reportedly suffering from illnesses such as sleep apnea, hypertension, diabetes, and major depressive disorder — not cancer

Claim: Following his arrest, medical findings confirmed that former House speaker Martin Romualdez has stage 4 cancer.

Rating: FALSE

Why we fact-checked this: A YouTube channel named “News Update Files” uploaded a video on September 9 claiming that Romualdez has stage 4 cancer.

Text on its thumbnail reads, “Stage 4 cancer!? Romualdez paktay [sic] na!?” (Stage 4 cancer!? Romualdez is already dead!?). It shows Romualdez lying in a hospital bed with a detainee shirt draped over him.

The video’s title reads, “Kapapasok lang! Breaking news! Romualdez paktay na! Confirmed! Tamba merong stage 4 cancer pala!”

(Just in! Breaking news! Romualdez is already dead! Confirmed! Turns out Tamba has stage 4 cancer!)

As of writing, the video has drawn over 4,400 views, 230 likes, and 60 comments.

The facts: There is no court filing, public hospital record, or credible news report confirming that Romualdez has cancer, whether stage 4 or otherwise. The lawmaker’s medical conditions, as cited in reports, concern other health issues.

Romualdez was arrested on September 7 over a P7.44-billion plunder case linked to alleged flood control kickbacks. Authorities served the warrant while he was confined at Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City. Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said that at the time of arrest, Romualdez was suffering from a cardiovascular event, unstable blood pressure, and an anxiety attack.

Because of his condition, authorities processed Romualdez at his hospital bedside rather than taking him to a police station. He was photographed lying down, with the detainee shirt draped over him and the booking sign positioned above him. (READ: How Martin Romualdez avoided jail by going to hospital)

His actual documented conditions are cardiovascular and neurologic in nature, not cancer. In his own manifestation asking the anti-graft court Sandiganbayan for continued hospital confinement, Romualdez cited coronary artery disease, diabetes, and primary hypothyroidism, among other ailments.

The court ordered his transfer to the Philippine General Hospital (PGH), where an independent assessment found that Romualdez has chronic coronary syndrome, hypothyroidism, sleep apnea, anxiety, and major depressive disorder.

PGH Medical Director Dr. Gerardo Legaspi, however, said that these conditions are under controlled medication and that the lawmaker is in stable condition.

Behind bars: The Sandiganbayan subsequently ordered Romualdez’s transfer to the Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory in Payatas on September 14 following the PGH doctors’ examination. Romualdez remains alive and in custody, with his official mugshots being released the following day.

Romualdez is accused of receiving kickbacks related to the flood control corruption scheme. The case also involves former Ako Bicol representative Elizaldy “Zaldy” Co and two private individuals. Co remains at large, while Romualdez has pleaded not guilty during his arraignment before the Sandiganbayan on September 16. – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com

Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.

World.title: Ombudsman flags DICT, begins fact-finding for ‘ghost internet’ projects
World.content:
The 'ghost internet' projects deal with government contracts where hardware and related software are bought by the government, but the software installed may be either outdated or fake, leading to project overpricing

MANILA, Philippines – The Office of the Ombudsman announced in a press briefing on Friday, September 18, that it was conducting a fact-finding mission on what it called “ghost internet” projects.

The “ghost internet” projects deal with government contracts where hardware and related software are bought by the government for billions of pesos, but the software installed within the devices purchased may be either outdated or fake, leading to project overpricing.

Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano said during the briefing, “Once the hardware — the machines, the routers — are delivered and passes inspection, everyone assumes the software that’s supposed to run on it is there as well. But nobody actually checks, and there comes the loophole.”

“A contractor can install cheaper, outdated, or even fake software while still charging the government full price for the real thing. Because nobody verifies the software after the hardware is approved, the overpricing goes undetected,” Clavano added.



It is only found out when systems break down or when somebody digs into the matter further. The investigation, Clavano said, will center around the DICT and will seek to answer four basic questions.

Were the contracted sites actually installed and are they working?

Was the government billed for connectivity and services that were never delivered?

Were the prices of hardware, software, and services reasonable or inflated?

Who approved, certified, or released payments for projects that were not delivered?

Clavano also said the scope of the investigation will deal with entirety of contracts related to DICT initiatives, but did not specify particulars as the fact-finding process is ongoing.

The Ombudsman, in the same press briefing, confirmed that graft complaints are now pending against members of the Villar family due to allegations related to PrimeWater Infrastructure Corporation. – Rappler.com

World.title: World View with Marites Vitug: Inside the fight against POGOs
World.content:
LIVE

Rappler editor-at-large Marites Vitug speaks to former PAOCC officials Winnie Quidato and Winston Casio about their book, The Rogue Compound: POGOs, Human Trafficking, and the Fight to Reclaim the Philippines

Bookmark this page to catch the discussion on Friday, September 18, at 6 pm!

MANILA, Philippines – Scam compounds linked to Philippine offshore gaming operators (POGOs) have become a major organized crime problem in the country, with human trafficking, online scams, and other criminal activities converging in the same operations.

Former Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC) officials Winnie Quidato and Winston Casio draw on their experience dismantling scam compounds in their new book, The Rogue Compound: POGOs, Human Trafficking, and the Fight to Reclaim the Philippines.

On Friday, September 18, Rappler editor-at-large Marites Vitug speaks to Quidato and Casio about how scam compounds took root in the Philippines, the challenges law enforcement faced in going after them, and what it takes to dismantle these criminal networks.

Quidato is a retired police officer with decades of experience in intelligence work. He spent three years working to dismantle scam compounds as PAOCC deputy executive director. Casio, meanwhile, is a crime analyst and educator who served as PAOCC spokesperson.

With the Anti-POGO Act now in place, do POGOs still operate underground?

Catch the interview on Thursday at 6 pm! – Rappler.com

World.title: FACT CHECK: Poa remains VP Sara’s counsel, defense spokesperson in impeachment trial
World.content:
Lawyer Michael Poa serves as Duterte's legal counsel and defense team spokesperson in her impeachment trial. He stepped down as the Office of the Vice President’s spokesperson in 2024.

Claim: Lawyer Michael Wesley Poa has vacated his post as Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesperson.

Rating: MISSING CONTEXT

Why we fact-checked this: The claim was posted on September 9 by the Facebook page “Balita at Kaalaman,” which has more than 219,000 followers. The post has reached over 1,800 reactions as of writing.

The post, labeled as “breaking news,” reads, “Atty Michael Poa binitawan na ni #SaraDuterte after kawawain sa harap ng publiko. Grabe ginagawa sayo niyang praning na amo mo atty.”

(Sara Duterte dropped Atty. Michael Poa after being humiliated in public. That paranoid boss of yours is really putting you through a lot, attorney.)

Two other posts, uploaded on September 2 and 7 respectively, mention that Poa has resigned as Duterte’s spokesperson.

A YouTuber by the channel name “Mike Cervera Vlog” also posted a live stream commentary on August 29 with the title “Atty. Michael Poa nag resign na?!” As of writing, it has reached over 180,000 views and 400 comments.

The posts circulated following reports on September 9 that Duterte appointed lawyer Paolo Panelo as the new spokesperson for the Office of the Vice President (OVP).

The facts: Poa already stepped down as Duterte’s spokesperson on November 5, 2024. However, he remains Duterte’s legal counsel and her defense team’s spokesperson in her impeachment trial. He himself confirmed this in a message to the media on the day Panelo’s appointment was announced.

In a September 10 interview on Bilyonaryo News Channel, Poa clarified his role as he addressed social media speculation that he had been replaced or removed from Duterte’s team.

In November 2024, Poa said the OVP pre-terminated his consultancy contract as spokesperson, describing the move as a “mutual decision.” He added that he could not fulfill his contract as spokesperson because he deemed it difficult to face the media without losing objectivity. At the time, Poa was a resource person in a House panel probe into the OVP’s alleged misuse of funds.

In appointing Panelo as its new spokesperson, the OVP said he will “serve as the official point of communication, representing the views and positions of the Vice President and engaging with the media and public on relevant matters.”

Prosecution’s hostile witness: On September 1, Poa temporarily stepped aside as counsel and spokesperson for the Vice President’s defense team to take the witness stand in the impeachment trial.

He became one of the prosecution’s hostile witnesses, called to testify on Article I of the impeachment articles concerning Duterte’s alleged misuse of confidential funds.

During the trial, Poa faced questions around the use of P112.5 million in confidential funds of the Department of Education (DepEd). In his testimony, Poa said that during his time as DepEd undersecretary and chief of staff, he prepared the agency’s response to the 2024 Commission on Audit findings on DepEd’s use of confidential funds.

However, he said that he was unaware that Duterte’s security officer Colonel Dennis Nolasco handled the funds.

He clarified that his involvement in the confidential funds issue only began when he received the audit memorandum, and that he relied on other officials’ reports to respond to COA’s inquiries on the use of the funds. – Lourence Angelo Marcellana/Rappler.com

World.title: Villar family faces graft complaints over PrimeWater contracts
World.content:
(1st UPDATE) In a statement, Manny Villar says they respect the legal process and will respond to the complaints at the proper time and forum

MANILA, Philippines – The Office of the Ombudsman confirmed on Friday, September 18, that graft complaints are now pending against members of the Villar family due to allegations related to PrimeWater Infrastructure Corporation.

Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano confirmed that the Ombudsman filed criminal and administrative complaints against Senators Mark and Camille, former senators Manny and Cynthia Villar, and businessman Paolo Villar for preliminary investigation.

Also included in the complaints are officers of PWIC, as well as local water district officials.

Preliminary investigation is the step of criminal proceedings where prosecutors decide if there’s enough evidence against the respondents. If there is, the prosecutors will indict the respondents and file cases with courts.

“[This is] for violation, of section 3(e) and 3(g) of [Republic Act No.] 3019, otherwise known as the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. This is the initial list, and there are still more water districts under investigation, and expectantly more cases in the pipelines,” Clavano said.

In a statement, Manny Villar said they respect the legal process and will respond to the complaints at the proper time and forum.

“We are confident that, once given the opportunity to examine the allegations and the evidence supporting them, we will be able to fully and properly defend our rights and address the matters raised against us,” Villar said.

“In the meantime, we ask that the legal process be allowed to take its course and that conclusions not be drawn before the parties have been afforded the opportunity to be heard,” he added.

Also included in the complaints are the following PrimeWater and local water district officials:

Fe Rebancos, PrimeWater president

Romeo Sabater, PrimeWater vice president

Enrico Pasumbal, Quezon Metropolitan Water district general manager

Guillermo Pili Jr., San Pedro Water District general manager

Juliet Ocampo, Trece Martires Water District general manager

According to the Ombudsman, the investigations stemmed from a report from the Office of the Government Corporate Counsel that showed that a total of 75 local water districts (LWDs) entered into joint venture agreements (JVA) with PrimeWater.

However, a report revealed that PrimeWater failed to supply uninterrupted water service and instead provided water that “allegedly failed to meet drinking water standards, among other complaints against the company.”

Other concerns also include questions on JVAs itself and PrimeWater’s deficient service, and how these happened under Mark Villar’s term as Department of Public Works and Highways secretary and Local Water Utilities Administration board of trustees Member.

The Ombudsman also noted that the Commission on Audit had flagged PrimeWater’s “non-payment for the utilization or consumption of materials and supplies inventory of the local water districts.”

“Considering the three (Quezon Metro, Trece Martires, and San Pedro, Laguna) areas, the total unpaid obligations of PWIC have reached P65,650,708.07,” said the Ombudsman.

The Villars are also facing a separate complaint with the Department of Justice for alleged violations of the Securities Regulation Code. The complaint, filed on January 30, is currently at the preliminary investigation level. – Rappler.com

World.title: News Digest: Rybakina’s US Open Triumph, Kazakhstan-South Korea Ties and Oil Export Strategy
World.content:
ASTANA – The Astana Times has selected articles from global media outlets covering Kazakhstan. This week’s foreign media digest highlights Elena Rybakina’s U.S. Open victory, strengthened Kazakhstan-South Korea cooperation, Astana Arena’s selection to host the 2028 UEFA Super Cup, and Kazakhstan’s efforts to diversify its oil export routes.

S. Korea, Kazakhstan sign MOU on preservation of historic sites linked to Korea’s independence movement

South Korea and Kazakhstan have signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to help better preserve historical sites in the Central Asian country that are linked to Korea’s independence movement against Japan’s 1910-45 colonial rule, Seoul’s veterans ministry said Wednesday, Yonhap reported on Sept. 16.

“Under the MOU, the two countries agreed to systematically preserve the historical records and cultural value of historical sites related to Korea’s independence movement while also strengthening academic exchanges. There are 25 historical sites related to Korea’s independence movement in the central Asian country, according to the ministry,” reads the article.

Seoul Cyber University chairman receives Kazakhstan’s Order of Dostyk

Lee Sang-kyun, chairman of Seoul Cyber University (SCU), received Kazakhstan’s Order of Dostyk, recognizing his contributions to expanding online education and promoting friendly cooperation between Korea and Kazakhstan, reported The Korea Times on Sept. 16.

Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, who visited Korea this week for the first Korea-Central Asia Summit, personally presented the order to Lee on Monday. The Order of Dostyk is one of Kazakhstan’s highest state honors, awarded to figures at home and abroad for contributions to peace, friendship, international cooperation and social harmony.

U.S. Open final: Elena Rybakina smothers Aryna Sabalenka to dethrone reigning champion

For the second time this year, Elena Rybakina is a Grand Slam champion after defeating Aryna Sabalenka. The 27-year-old from Kazakhstan toppled Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 on Saturday in the U.S. Open final, denying Sabalenka’s bid to win the tournament for a third straight year, The New York Times reported on Sept. 13.

“It is Rybakina’s first U.S. Open title, and her third Grand Slam title overall. It means she leaves the tournament as both the champion and the new world No. 1: Rybakina will replace Sabalenka at the top of women’s tennis on Monday,” reads the article.

Astana Arena in the capital of Kazakhstan selected to host 2028 UEFA Super Cup

The prestigious match, UEFA Super Cup, will take place at the Johan Cruyff Arena in Amsterdam, Netherlands, in 2027, before passing the baton to Astana Arena in Astana, Kazakhstan, in 2028. Kazakhstan has obtained the chance to host such a major match, marking a historic first for the country, Euronews reported on Sept. 15.

The decision was made and officially announced by the UEFA Executive Committee. Since 2013, the Super Cup venue has changed every year, moving to a new location each time. Kazakhstan has obtained the chance to host such a major match, marking a historic first for the country. For the uninitiated, the UEFA Super Cup is a single-match curtain-raiser where the Champions League and Europa League winners meet.

Kazakhstan is upgrading its oil export strategy: Here’s how

Astana is looking for more ways to move its oil. Russia, its principal export outlet, is rife with disruptions. Damage to the Caspian Pipeline Consortium’s (CPC) Black Sea terminal in November 2025 suppressed exports into early 2026, while the recent July attacks on tankers threatened roughly 1.5 million barrels per day, writes Joseph Shumunov for EU Reporter on Sept. 15.

The vulnerability would not be so enormous if 80% of Kazakh oil exports did not move through the CPC terminal near Novorossiysk. But is Kazakhstan merely searching for emergency alternatives amid instability? Or is this a transformation it has been preparing for? The answer is consequential: Kazakhstan is attempting a wholesale upgrade of its oil-export strategy, one befitting a rising regional power. It is moving from rational efficiency toward strategic resilience, from accepting routes toward shaping them, and from concentrated dependence toward managed interdependence.

World.title: Italy, Central Asia Launch B5+Italy Platform to Expand Regional Business Ties
World.content:
ASTANA – Government and business representatives from Central Asia and Italy convened on Sept. 16 in Astana for the launch of the B5+Italy platform aimed at turning growing political engagement into investment, industrial cooperation and stronger trade links across the region.

The forum in Astana brought together government officials and businesses from Italy, Kazakhstan, the Kyrgyz Republic, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan, with discussions focused on connectivity, sustainable growth and new opportunities for companies operating across Central Asia.

The meeting follows the first Central Asia-Italy summit at the leaders’ level, held in Astana in May 2025, when Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and the presidents of the five Central Asian states agreed to deepen cooperation across trade, investment, transport, energy and other sectors.

The platform, proposed by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, is designed to complement the political dialogue in C5+1 format by giving businesses a more direct role in shaping economic cooperation.

Italian Undersecretary of State for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Maria Tripodi said the new business format was intended to give that political dialogue an economic dimension.

“We consider that today’s meeting is important because it is the beginning of a new era. (…) We want to transform the political dialogue into investments, partnerships and new opportunities for our countries,” Tripodi told the forum participants.

“It is the companies, in fact, that are subject to transform the political relationship into a more solid one, investing time and effort,” she said.

A dynamic market

Addressing the gathering, Kazakh Minister of Trade and Integration Arman Shakkaliyev said the forum gives an opportunity to Italian companies to approach Central Asia increasingly as a regional market rather than five isolated economies.

“Today, Central Asia is a market with a rapidly growing economy,” said the minister. “For Italian businesses, today’s forum represents an opportunity to work with the entire region and to expand production and market presence across several countries simultaneously.”

He said Central Asia should increasingly be viewed as an interconnected economic space where companies can establish production in one country while reaching consumers and supply chains across several neighboring markets.

For Kazakhstan, the regional format also offers an opportunity to use existing business infrastructure with Italy more broadly. Shakkaliyev highlighted the Kazakh-Italian Trade House that opened in Almaty earlier this year, saying it could serve not only bilateral commerce but wider links between Italian companies and Central Asia.

Growing interest from businesses

The push toward a regional format is also coming from companies and business associations that have traditionally worked through bilateral Kazakhstan-Italy ties. Marco Beretta, president of the Italian-Kazakh Trade Association, said the leaders’ summit in May 2025 convinced businesses that cooperation could be expanded beyond the two countries.

“In the last three years, we have been working very hard in order to promote collaboration between Italy and Kazakhstan,” Beretta told The Astana Times. “But after the visit of our prime minister last year in May, we understood that a much wider scope of work can be executed.”

He described Central Asia as an increasingly important economic link for Europe and said the expansion toward a five-country regional format represented a significant shift. Beretta said the association now wants to expand its Kazakh-Italian business forum into a broader Central Asian platform while keeping Kazakhstan as its base.

Diversifying trade structure

The forum comes at a time as Italy expands its economic engagement with Central Asia, with Kazakhstan accounting for a large share of that relationship. Italy was Kazakhstan’s third-largest trading partner last year, with bilateral trade reaching almost $17 billion in 2025, according to Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Trade and Integration. Trade reached $9.79 billion in January-July this year, including $9 billion in Kazakh exports to Italy and $789.6 million in imports.

But Shakkaliyev said maintaining high trade volumes alone was not enough. He pointed to the big role of commodities in the current structure of bilateral commerce.

Kazakhstan is seeking to expand exports of higher-value goods and estimates that it has an additional $307.5 million in export potential on the Italian market, particularly in metallurgy, petrochemicals, food products, chemicals and machinery.

Shakkaliyev said Kazakhstan was interested in changing the structure of trade by increasing exports of processed and higher-value products. He pointed to opportunities in agriculture, chemicals, manufacturing and industrial cooperation, while Tripodi emphasized Italian expertise in engineering, machinery and advanced industrial technologies.

This ambition reflects a broader challenge for Central Asian economies of moving from exports of raw materials toward local processing, manufacturing and bigger participation in international value chains.

Connectivity as central theme

Transport and logistics featured prominently in the forum as Central Asian states seek to strengthen links between Asian and European markets. Kazakhstan, which has invested around $35 billion in this area in the past 15 years, has promoted its position along transcontinental trade routes, particularly the Middle Corridor across the Caspian Sea. The Middle Corridor, formally known as the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route, links China and Central Asia with Europe through the Caspian Sea, the South Caucasus and Türkiye.

Shakkaliyev said the region’s transport infrastructure could provide Italian producers and investors with access not only to Central Asian markets but also to wider international supply chains.

Tripodi said Italy was ready to share technology and experience to support Kazakhstan’s economic diversification, pointing to logistics as one area for cooperation.

“Our connectivity depends on growth and on being connected in a safe, self-sufficient way in large international markets,” she said. “We want Italy to be at the same time the driver of this new road to Europe and also the protagonist of its realization. Our companies are ready to contribute.”

Diversifying economic ties

Beretta pointed to logistics, agriculture, technology and petrochemicals as areas where Italian companies could work across the region. He also tied diversification to the development of higher-value production in Kazakhstan rather than continued reliance on raw-material exports.

“We need to create added value,” Beretta said.

Beretta also said one project under discussion is the development of a logistics hub in Kazakhstan accompanied by local production, including sustainable aviation fuel. He said such projects could also be part of a wider push into decarbonization, renewable power generation, sustainable development and water treatment.

“Decarbonization, power generation in a green way, sustainable development and water treatment are very important for Central Asia,” he said, stressing that Italian companies could bring technologies and industrial experience in those areas.

According to Tripodi, Italian companies have built extensive presence in oil and gas, but they are also looking to expand into renewable energy, critical minerals and areas linked to energy transition.

Shakkaliyev also noted Italy’s experience with small and medium-sized industrial companies could be particularly relevant for Central Asia, where governments are seeking investment that creates production capacity and jobs.

In her remarks, Tripodi noted the region offered a large and relatively young market of around 80 million people, combined with energy resources, critical materials and a strategic position between Europe and Asia. The country sees potential for its companies in sectors where Central Asian governments are trying to move further up value chains, she said.

Tripodi said Italian companies could contribute through design, engineering and industrial technologies as Central Asian economies seek greater diversification.

World.title: Apple TV Officially Launches in Kazakhstan
World.content:
ASTANA — Apple TV has officially launched in Kazakhstan, giving users direct access to Apple Original films and series for the first time.

The streaming service is included in all iCloud+ plans alongside Apple Arcade, with no separate Apple TV subscription required.

The basic iCloud+ plan costs 499 tenge (US$1) per month and includes 50 gigabytes (GB) of cloud storage.

The service is available on Apple devices, compatible smart TVs, gaming consoles and other platforms.

World.title: Expert: Astana’s Financial Center Rating Rises 18 Points on Structural Progress
World.content:
ASTANA – Astana’s eight-place rise in the Global Financial Centers Index 40 (GFCI 40) should ultimately be measured by whether growing international confidence translates into more investment, deeper capital markets and greater cross-border financial activity, Bakhtiyar Tleubekov, chairman of the Management Board of Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC Authority), told The Astana Times on Sept. 18.

In the 40th edition of the Global Financial Centers Index, Kazakhstan’s capital ranked 57th among 117 financial centers worldwide, climbing eight places from 65th. Astana’s rating increased by 18 points, from 684 to 702.

Astana retains regional leadership

The city retained its leading position in Eastern Europe and Central Asia, which it has held for more than three years. Astana was followed by Cyprus, which ranked 72nd globally, and Warsaw, which placed 78th.

Astana’s rise came against a 1.09% decline in the average rating of financial centers in Eastern Europe and Central Asia. It was also named among the ten financial centers survey participants expected to play a more significant role in the global financial system over the next two to three years, ranking ninth with 45 mentions.

In the separate FinTech ranking, Astana rose four places from 55th to 51st.

“Astana’s eight-place rise and continued regional leadership send an important signal of growing confidence in the AIFC and Kazakhstan among the international financial community. For us, a position in the ranking is not an end in itself, but an independent assessment of the work we are consistently pursuing: improving the legal and regulatory environment, developing capital markets and financial technologies, and expanding international ties,” said AIFC Governor Renat Bekturov.

From ranking to capital flows

“The real measure of success is whether growing international confidence translates into more investment, deeper capital markets, more international financial institutions operating in Kazakhstan, and greater cross-border financial activity,” Tleubekov said.

According to him, over the next two to three years, the priority is to reinforce the conditions that international investors value most: political and macroeconomic stability, a predictable and transparent regulatory environment, consistent application of the law, and effective protection of investor rights.

Astana and Kazakhstan also need to continue strengthening their role as a regional gateway connecting international capital with opportunities across Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.

“Kazakhstan’s geographic position and growing role in trans-Caspian transport and logistics create an opportunity to complement physical connectivity with financial connectivity,” he said.

Structural progress and international confidence

Tleubekov noted that the GFCI combines assessments from financial-sector professionals with quantitative indicators from more than 80 external sources covering the business environment, human capital, infrastructure, financial-sector development and reputation.

“Therefore, an 18-point increase cannot be attributed solely to improved perception, nor can it be explained by any single indicator,” he said.

He attributed Astana’s performance to both external conditions and structural progress, including Kazakhstan’s relative political and economic stability, regulatory continuity and openness to international investment.

The AIFC has been consistently developing a legal and regulatory framework based on international standards, independent dispute-resolution institutions, capital-market infrastructure, fintech and digital-asset regulation, and mechanisms for international and regional investors.

“Ultimately, progress should be measured not only by rankings, but by new investment, international companies choosing the AIFC, and new opportunities for Kazakhstan’s businesses,” Bekturov said.

The GFCI is published twice a year by the Z/Yen Group in partnership with the China Development Institute and assesses financial centers across five areas: business environment, financial sector development, infrastructure, human capital and reputation.

Continuing the conversation

The Astana Times has been following the AIFC’s development and Kazakhstan’s evolving role in the international financial system through its coverage and interviews with AIFC leadership.

At the recent Astana Finance Days, Bekturov joined discussions on the future of finance and Kazakhstan’s role in the next digital frontier.

The AIFC also recently shared the results of its first 10 years with The Astana Times team, offering a closer look at the centre’s development, growing international presence and priorities for the next decade. Also watch our YouTube interview with AIFC leadership.
